Noticed there are a lot of negative reviews, remeber more people are likely to write a review if they had a bad experience than a good.
Review written after game completion:
Wowee what a game, definately ranks up there with the greats only Mafia 2 and the original Godfather game could reach (what a coincidence they happen to be mafia related). If you loved Mafia 2 as much as I did, I am nearly 100% sure that you will love this just as much, even though some things aren't as good, the things that are better make up for it.
I will update this review on a second playthrough which i certainly will do when new features come out/ after DLC releases wherein I will try to make notes...maybe.
Lets start with the cons, cos there aren't that many in my opinion:
Saves: There is only one save file, so you have to start again if you want to play through it again, no keeping a 100% save / collectable collecting save like I sometimes do with games I really enjoy
Customisation: In short, there is none, Lincoln has only one outfit (however he wears different things during a couple of missions, then changes back) and you cannot buy or change these (In a free content update there will be outfits added but as of writting there is nothing), cars cannot be customised and there is only a list of 6 cars you can own (9 with the family kickback pack), and no weapon customisation either, but there are a fair amount of guns to choose from.
Gameplay: Somewhat repetative, the main bulk of the game consists of going to location and shooting/sneaking into the location and interrogating/killing someone or blowing something up, there are very few classic missions such as with the layout of Mafia 2, however once an area is controlled a few of the missions that involve taking out the boss of that region are more in fitting with the classic mission style. Also Police dont really care in his game, speeding and so on just doesnt matter, sometimes even shotting people around them doesnt matter, and civilians just dont usually care about dead people and after a bit of screaming after a shootout they go back to their business.
Accuracy: A few other locations are listed other than New Bordeux, however these use the names of their real life counter parts i.e Las Vegas, Dallas etc, but not New Orleans which seemed a bit weird to me. Probably some other inaccuracies but I didnt find them.
Combat: Sneaking seems much easier than just going in guns blazing which in my opinion is a shame because it meant I didnt change up my play style very much. Also, no real hand to hand combat, you can punch but its just a single button, hold for brutal attack and very rarely an enemy will try to punch you back and you can press another button to counter and insta kill them.
Bugs: At the time of writting there are many graphical glitches and I have encountered a moment or two where my car got stuck inside a wall or truck, and one time when a character I had to fllow got stuck outside a door, but the worst thing that I had to do was reload a checkpoint so nothing ground breaking. My game aso crashed to desktop about 4 times during the entire playthrough.
I think thats about it so now pros:
Gameplay: Game is blooming fun, although the gameplay can be repetative its an enjoyable repetition.
Accuracy: There is a lot of racism, in some parts very over the top, but this is a good thing as it refelcts the nature of the time, as the opening to the game says it would be an insult to the people who have gone through it or are goign through it to pretend it never happened. There are no gun stores which at first felt a bit unimmersive, but then I remembered black people were not allowed guns at the time so realised it was actually at least partly for accuracy reasons.
Driving: I played on simulation mode, I found this to be basically an improved version of Mafia 2's driving which is exactly what I wanted, no real floaty feeling, and just difficult enough so that when you drift around a corner and narrowly avoid a car you feel like a badass. If you loved Mafia 2's driving, you won't be sorry. I was worried when they started calling the driving "cinematic" but as soon as I got in my first car I was no longer worried.
Combat: I played with a controller (because games with getting in and out of cars are good with controllers and being able to walk instead of always run really helps immersion) with aiming assist off (because thats how a  mafia game should be played, also the aiming assist felt too strong even on low and I struggled getting of quick shots accurately where I wanted them). The AI, both friendly and enemy are amazing, you get flanked and the AI try to work together sometimes to get around you meaning that sitting in cover all the time doesnt really work, you have to move around too. Furthermore the game feels like a Scorsese movie, which is perfect for the theme, lots of blood and sometime when you shoot people with real powerful guns, or point blank they fall back a good distance, far enough to be great to look at and feel powerful but not so far it looks stupid. If you dont want takedowns to be non lethal you can change it in the options menu according to the game, but I never felt the need to check because I didnt think it fit with Lincolns motive (innocents and seemingly police still get non lethaly takendown however so dont worry).
Story: This part is the best part of the whole game, while the over arching story of bad guy tries to kill you kill him back is somewhat cliche, the writting, voice acting and directing are all the sort of quality you rarely even see in top quality films, on top of this the (very minor spoiler about style of storytelling, with no story spoilers)
. Fan of Vito? He's in this too, as well as the absolute
resolution of Joe, as well as 2 other people you take on who have their own backstory, and a person under each of those who also have decent stories to tell. (Ending spoiler)
I think that's all for now, or at least as much as I can bother with, I dont think I even wrote this much for essays I did in school.
TL;DR, if you liked Mafia 2 I think you will love this, if you didnt but you love immersive, story driven games based in a sandbox open world a la GTA, you will likely love this. If you love games like COD, or expect GTA I think you might be disaapointed.
Well done to Hanger 13, an amazing experience and I can't wait for the future updates and looking forward even more so to their next venture, whnever it may be.

This is NOT AT ALL like Fallout 1 and 2 or similar classic CRPGs which offer significant choices and freedom, interesting dialogue, chances to use your creativity.
It's mechanical in the most boring way. You march linearly through a sequence of mostly empty areas. In each area, you do the same tedious and repetitive click-and-wait, which is all minor variations on the following minigame: find box, disarm trap [wait], disarm alarm [wait], unlock lock [wait], unlock tumbler [wait]. The waiting really is excessive. If you accidentally click things in the wrong order, which is guaranteed to happen since the click-wait dance is so boring, the box blows up or the alarm goes off. When you succeed, you get some minor loot. Which you must hold on to forever, because there is only one container in the entire game that you can put things in, and the game tells you things are junk when they might be useful.
Skills are all for boring skill checks like this; too few points, and you'll keep failing and waiting over and over, or have to take the long route through the area. That's too bad, since skills are your only way of interacting with the world outside combat.
Occasionally an area contains a friendly NPC. I guarantee that NPC has nothing interesting to say, and don't expect deep dialogue trees with important and rewarding decisions. Even the writing is boring. Just click all the topics until they go away to update quest status. Then go to some other area, do same tedious boxes-and-combat dance, come back to turn in quest for reward. Your reward is to level up and increase the mandatory weapon and box-opening skills. These are also illusory choices, because if you put points into the wrong skills, you will just be waiting more. It turns out there's one optimal way to make a character, this is impossible to determine before you have played the game or copied the perfect recipe, and if you didn't do it, the game is even more tedious. Unlike Fallout, you can't make weird characters like a a low-intelligence talker character or a nonviolent sleazeball work out. Just restart and build the character in the combat-oriented way you are forced to do.
What this leaves is a ton of unavoidable turn-based combat - which is decent, though simplistic; it mainly tests whether you put enough points into the right gun skills, because several of the gun skills are really not worthwhile.
Please do not buy this game unless turn-based combat is your primary interest. It's a "tactics" game. If you expect anything else, you'll be disappointed. If what you want is an RPG with choices, run away. There are no real choices. Your choices (such as they are) are morally 1-dimensional, you can't affect the politics or world in any interesting way, and it's not really possible to be bad or even strange. The only thing it is possible to be is a character which marches through the predetermined missions shooting things as intended.

Dispite a few minor flaws, this game is fantastic. The graphics, audio, and gameplay are all very high quality. The player forges their own story, with unique enemies and allies, in a world shaped by the player's decisions. There are 5 maps for the player to explore and fight in, which is a large improvement for the 2 maps of the last game.
While there are loot boxes, you recieve many for free or for completing missions, specifically in the "Vendetta Missions" where you avenge another player by killing the captain who killed them. Loot boxes are not forced upon you in any way, and I really don't understand why everyone is complaining about them. The claims that it is almost impossible to complete the final act without them are complete BS, as I'm having no trouble beating it at max difficulty.
My only major criticism for this game is the difficulty, as I have not found the highest difficulty to be very hard, though it is still considerably more diffucult than both normal difficulty and the difficulty of Shadow of Mordor. It may just be that I am good at this game.
I have had a lot of fun playing this, and it has been both a game and an experience to me. It saddens me that so many people are upset over the microtransactions because I really feel like this is the best game of 2017.

I read a lot of complaints about this game, that make little to no sense if you ask me.
People complain about micro payments, you dont need to buy anything, the wasteland and quests provide for everything you want to find/own, so paying for things, is optional.
Others claim this game forces you to come back every 5 minutes because of the resource gather system, this too isnt correct thinking, when you are not in the game, the power/water/food supply, does not drop under the minimum required amount of said goods. So, your dwellers wont starve if you have not played for 2 days, it would not make sense if it was the case now, would it?
And yet others complain that their dwellers die of lack of water or food, and that too is ridiculous, just make sure you got enough dwellers working the cafeteria(s), water refineree(s) and most importantly, the generator rooms, without power, other important rooms may stop functioning, and you can run out of water/food that way.
Also, make sure you add dwellers to jobs, that they are meant for, look at a dweller's stats before you assign him or her to a room, for example, if you have a dweller with 1 S(trenght) and 4 P(erception), you dont want that dweller to work in the generator rooms because those demand S(trenght) so instead, you send that dweller to the water refinery because that room demands P(erception), the higher the skill level of a dweller, the better he or she is suited for tasks that demand those skills, it speeds up the process of said rooms.
Ok review time, is this an amazing game? hmm, i guess that would be pushing it, but it sure is a fun game, looks good, has a million references to current and previous fallout games, with patience you can get all those items and dwellers from grinding the game itself, no cash needed.
Unlike what some people try to claim, this game is perfect for casual play, but also for constant play.
Questing is fun to do, exploring yields a lot of nice goodies as well, especially the longer you let a dweller explore the wastelands, the trick to do this succesfully is to make sure they go out there with a high damage weapon, and at least 25 stimpacks + say 10 or so, radaway, get them an outfit that gives them a bonus on strenght, perception, endurance and/or luck (there are a great variety of outfits, some with 1 added bonus, others with 2 or more) and also make sure the dweller you send, has decent levels of these skills, then you're set, and can send a dweller out for days at a time (actual days).
Do keep in mind, that whenever there is a fight (raiders invading, radroaches, molrats, gouls, deathclaws) that you dont need to do the fighting yourself, the dwellers will do this (if they have weapons) but you will have to apply stimpacks and radaway to keep the dwellers alive during a fight (same in quests), an icon will appear above the dweller when low on health, click it and he/she will use a stimpack or radaway, just make sure they have good weapons and gear.
But all in all, this game demands patience, and some people dont like to wait, thats 80% of the negative reactions on here i guess ;)

游戏画面带给我们的是满满艺术色彩的视觉效果，游戏性带给我们的是使用了比较异想天开的超能力，整个游戏带给我们的就是一个令人语味深长的故事，比较推荐喜欢冒险解谜类游戏的玩家不应错过过这样的一款游戏。怎么说呢，奇异人生的画面非常精美，明亮温暖的色彩也更吸引人。无论是校园还是城镇或是郊外，日常柔和温暖的光感好像是制作组有意添加的滤镜。当暴风雨来袭的时候，雨水即刻冲刷了油画般的风景，你可以清晰看到水滴打湿了周围的一切，冰冷和寒意也透过屏幕径直吹进玩家心里。笔者最喜欢游戏对于风的刻画，虚线与实线的勾画配合加深的灰度，风的轨迹就这样不失违和的呈现了眼前。若现实中的风也能这样看到轨迹，应该也和游戏中一样美吧。此外，像这样的互动电影游戏，人物自然也是游戏中的一大亮点。像麦克斯，维多利亚，内森和沃伦等游戏中的角色设置虽然平凡，但是其形象反而如同你曾经相处过的同学一般鲜活，角色代入上也毫无障碍。随着用鼠标来控制时间倒退，在改变人生轨迹的过程当中，我们作为玩家也深深的和游戏融为了一体。整体对这款游戏的评价是挺高的，画面很赞，音乐很赞，值得推荐的一款游戏吧。

In all seriousness, though, Civ 3 certainly delivers. You'll most definitely have a fun time, with all these hilarious moments appearing left and right.
The advisors actually have a use, and they have expressions, unlike Civ 4 and 5. (The Science Advisor is literally Sid Meier btw)
There's whole government systems as opposed to civics. Means you can't fine-tune your government, but it takes a bit of load off your shoulders if you're not into figuring out what civics you want.
Also, spearman vs. tank scenarios don't happen *that* often. 118 hours in at the time of writing, and RNG hasn't pulled any serious BS on me.
The only real downside that sticks out to me is the loading lag between each turn that builds up late-game when you play multiplayer matches. That isn't too significant, though, since if you can sit through 2 minutes straight of nothing but an AI doing carpet bombing runs on your capital, you can survive an extra 4 seconds of loading time.
This was a wonderful Christmas gift I got from a good friend of mine. I would most definitely buy the game for someone else, too.

This is a tower defense game, and in that regard, the game is good, but doesn't have any particular aspect that separates it from it's competitors. The concept seems fun: you are the commander of a human body immunity system, and you have to defend it in various levels, each in a different organ or muscle. The threats represent real life diseases such as angina, flu, cold, nichotin, cholestor, stonekid and even cancer. But when you play it, you'll quickly forget about all that, and it's just another tower defense game. But it's a good one. There's 18 levels each with 3 difficulties, but in practice they mostly play differently, so you have about 50 levels that feel different, even with the same layout. Each enemy type has different characteristics, and will require a different strategy. And there's plenty of tower types to build and upgrade, and they all play differently. There's also a hero that you can command, and other small upgrades to buy. Even if it's nothing new, there's plenty of content here to check. On another note, this game will no longer be patched, despite some bugs still present. But the game is completely playable, and i haven't had any real issues with it that prevented me from enjoying it. If you're worried, none of achievements are broken.

Microtransactions alone would justify my bad review, but let's look past that for once.
The game is really good in certain areas, but it mainsly sticks to ball-sucking and mediocrity. Couple that with great ideas on paper, which turn out to suffer from bad execution, you're left with the bittersweet taste in your mouth that is Shadow of War.
The story is okay-ish, and what's to note here is that the story is really around 5 sub-stories, not necessarily affecting the plot in any way. Some are introductions for cool scenarios (the balrog one) while others just leave you with a sense of incompletion and bafflement. In particular, I'm talking about the Gondor quests, which litterally only lead up to a typical rescue-mission with two of the main characters with a 1 minute-long cutscene at the end of it, which is the last time you'll see either of them. There's no recognition of player, as they just striaght up run away from you, despite you being the source of their every success throughout the whole game. And this happens about midway through the story. The rest of the quests are fine, they vary in entertainment and repetition, but none of them really stand out.
The Nemesis system is obviously upgraded for the sequel and there are a lot of cool suprises throughout your time with it. Also, the interaction between you and the orcs, or the between the orcs themselves, sometimes lead to some pretty dope scenarios. Ambush, betrayal, life-saver, blood-brothers; these are the features that keep the system feel alive and fresh. However, when that is said and done, this is supposed to be the core of the game, and sure, it is, but the whole formula feel stale after a while, and suddenly you find yourself vaulting over 50 orcs looking for arrows, because pinning this motherf*cker is apparently the only f*cking thing that will get me an opening. The unique traits and personalities of the orcs feel few and far between (I've met one necromancer my whole playthrough). Your normal orcs, you basically don't care about unless they are epic+, or have a cool hat. Many of them start to sound the same and even crack the same jokes or one-liners (f*ck you and your pride, Buroq the Unashamed). Especially when completing missions with them, but it becomes very apparent when fighting in the pits, which leads me to the next point.
The grind is un-f*cking-bearable, so let's break it up for ya: when the story ends somewhat abruptly you're faced with the endgame, or the Shadow Wars, which consists of 20 bloody sieges on 4 of your fortresses over 10 stages. Each siege requires you to gather orcs, level them up countless times in the pits to make them viable warchiefs or bodyguards, and then spend in-game currency on fortress upgrades to counter the attackers.
This sucks because:
Why not automate the cr*p so you can do cool stuff while your orcs harden themselves? Doesn't make sense I have to actively watch the little sh*ts for them to get better.
These are my gripes with the game. My completionistic nature drove me 44 hours into it, but it did not feel worthwhile. It's not a bad game per se, but I don't really get the satisfaction I had hoped.

I would not recommend this game to anyone unless they just love the Arkham Knight style combat system.
Orc intros become beyond tedious by Act III and you have no way of skpping or disabling them.
Often times beating Orc Captains in the end game comes down to hitting start mid battle, going to the character screen and adjusting ability effects so you target the captain's weakness or at least avoid their immunities.
Act III might as well be one long cutscene, it's a joke otherwise.
Act IV is just a needlessly long grind that combined with orc intros and the other negative aspects of the game make it an absolute chore to finish, all for the 'true ending' which is an ending that is questionable at best.
By the end there are so many captains and orcs on the battlefield that unless your a robot you simply can't counter or avoid hits, so you find yourself cheesing fights with drakes/graugs, explosions and guerilla tactics.
Lastly a problem I thought people were joking about in posts and reviews:  If you get hit by RNG and are stuck in a quicktime event then a new captain spawns or cutscene plays, you will fail the quicktime event, it continues to play while you can't perform any inputs.  This happened to me twice in the 8th stage of ACT IV.
Least of all my concerns is the microtransaction system, it just goes to show that game companies have fully bought into the new system.  Let's be clear, I played on nemesis difficulty and never found a need to use the crates, sure they would have been helpful but with using in game fight pits and nemesis missions you just don't need them.
If i could give it a rating out of ten, i would say six, wait until it's price reduced or released with a GOTY edition.

Having bought the original version of FSX way back in 2007, I have mixed feeling about FSX:SE. On the one hand, it is much better optimised than the original boxed FSX, which required manual tweaks to run properly. That being said, FSX:SE is not without its faults, and is a particular nuisance when it comes to third-party hardware and software. Certain errors that were present in the original version of FSX are still present in FSX:SE, which further highlights that this is basically a re-launch of the original 2006 game.
If you dont own any version of FS yet, I would highly reccomend this game. It runs well on high settings on my 5 year old potato and functioning multiplayer is definitely worth it. In the case you own the original boxed FSX, I would advise you to think about buying this full price. Take into account the amount of free- and payware addons you own and that some may not work in FSX:SE.
Overall, I enjoyed FSX:SE. It has its faults, some more annoying than others, but with a decent computer it should run just fine

If you like short and sweet stories then Virginia has a lot to love. A story setup and small town vibe of Twin Peaks crossed with the cinematic jump cutting from Thirty Flights of Loving. There's not much interactivity, but the editing of the scenes, the art direction, animation and music all really work great together. I cannot understate how beautiful the game and the music is.
Similar to Thirty Flights of Loving there's no dialogue, but the staging of the scenes, use of images, environmental cues and character performance are plenty to show you what's going on. It really goes to show you how much story you can convey without resorting to exposition and dialogue.
In David Lynch fashion the narrative can be mysterious or obtuse, but in a way that makes me want to replay it so that I can pick out clues or hints that I missed the first time through.
If you're the sort of person who's first questions are "How long is it?" or "But is it a game?" Then this likely isn't your cup of tea, but if you like short narrative games then you'll love it!

Broken Age is a modern adventure game with throwbacks to the past and - at least for me - an ideal fusion of both worlds.
Background: I'm not a backer, so the game didn't have to live up to a specific promise for me. I used to play adventure games back in the 90ies. I waited until Act 2 was out, before I started playing Act 1&2.
There's so much to love. The art style is amazing, charming, well thought out and manages to create a whole real world, partly made out of yarn. Yay! The character design and animations are great. The puzzles in Act 1 are easy enough to welcome newcomers to the genre and quickly ramp up in Act 2 to provide a real challenge and with that a real feeling of accomplishment upon solving them. There are always hints to be found. The writing is brightly witty. The voice acting is top of the line. The "plot twist" at the end of Act 1 genuinely surprised me and had me uttering "what the f..." maybe 10+ times out loud in a row. Well done.
I really liked the transition into Act 2: the character reveals, the expansion of the world and the fact that you had to solve puzzles with things introduced in Act 1. I felt even more at home in Act 2: switching between the characters felt like switching between the characters in Zak McKracken, constructing
reminded me of the Monkey Island swordmaster insults. I didn't miss the verb interface at all.
The only complaint I have is, that you can't load straight from a running game, you have to save+exit to the main menu first. That's it.
I'd strongly recommend Broken Age to everyone interested in puzzles, art or humor. It's a monument for what can be achieved with love, talent and dedication.

I was a huge fan of the previous version, Shadow of Mordor and this version took it to the next level. It was improved on every single aspect so I totally recommend it. Not only to fans of the previous version, but also for people that never played the series. The story stands on itself, you won't miss much, but it deffinitely helps if you played the first, The story goes on where Shadow of Mordor ended.
All this being said, with new content and goodies also came new irritations. So I still recommend it to everyone, but there are certainly things that could have been done much better. Lets take a look at the pro's and con's.
-Camera! Seriously it is the most annoying part of this game. 70% of the time the 3rd person camera is fine, but in 30% of the times you'll be adjusting it with your right stick just to see where you want to go. This is infuriating after the third time you die because your camera was pointing in the completely wrong direction. This should be fixes ASAP in an update.
-Sometimes, thanks to the nemesis system a boss becomes almost unbeatable on your own. Especially the bosses with the No Chance perk (you don't get to have the option to deflect the final blow) are VERY hard in certain circumstances and when they are high level. If you take into consideration some bosses have caragors, spear throwers and berserkers with them while they on themselves also have accumulated strong defences and can kill you with 3 blows it can be very hard to beat them. It took me a while to figure out you have another option to kill your arch enemy and that is by sending 1-3 of your own captains to kill him. You can assist if you want. But before I figured this out, it was very hard and often irritating.
-Once you reach chpt 4, the game is much easier/faster if you invested in Loot boxes. It's a simple fact. If you bought your orcs, it will be faster to have strong up to par captains for the challenge at hand. (but that's it, I'll come back to loot boxes in the pro section!)
-In Shadow of Mordor, every time you got a skill point, you became stronger either way. In shadow of War you must chose your build. This means if you get a skill point you can invest it in 1 main power, which has then 2-3 sub posers. But unlike SoM you need to choose ONE of the subpowers, so you can't have them all. For some that may be intruiging, but I miss the feeling of becoming all powerfull like you had in SoM. In Shadow of War you'll sometimes change your subpowers to meet the challenge in front of you (like a nemessis with very specific defences). I simply find that annoying and wish it was like SoM: every skill point accumulates your strength.Additionally, if you complete the game you have surplus skill points that you can't spend (yet) which imho is poor logic, as now we have a constant reminder we have unspent skill points, but we can't spend them...
-I'll combine my final two irritations: Cut scenes and targetting. Every time a captain enters the fray, a cutscene starts his introduction. This is in the midlle of the fight, where the camera turns towards him, and stays on him after the intro. This was awesome in SoM, but in SoW you will face many captains at the same time, many times! Now without a targetting system (Come ON, this can not be hard to implement!!!) you will constantly lose focus on the boss you where fighting. You will also die because of this or captains will manage to escape because of this, and your own captains will die during sieges because of this. A targetting system that holds your boss during cut scenes) would solve all this instantly... This is without a doubt the real negative in this game.
Now the pro's!
+ Story. Excellent addition to SoM story and for example the movies. Especially the story of Shelob got me intruiged. Very well done again and I can't wait for the DLC stories! Only downside: it was a bit short, they tried to dragg it along with the 10 stage shadow wars, but take those away and it's pretty short.
+ Orc duels. A very cool addition is to have your orcs fight vs enemy orcs in the arena. Especially since you can train your own orcs to a certain degree. I honestly had a lot of fun cheering for my favorite hand made Olog fighting other captains! (You can't intervene a duel, so all you can do is spectate)
+ Training your orcs. You can train your orcs by giving them missions so they level up, or by using loot boxes that contain training orders. So you can give your captains caragors, fire weapons, resistance to cetain dmg etc... It's a very cool addition especially combined to the duels in the arenas.
+ new skills like double jump, shadow dominate, ressurect fallen enemies/friends are all very nice.
+ Gear. You can collect and level legendary gear. It's a nice addition and it makes you want to collect the entire set. Upgrading gear is done by doing a certain mission, like dominate an orc from the marauder tribe, higher then lvl 30-40-55-60. And you want a full set for the extra bonusses so it's additional content, that makes you stronger.
+ Once you finished the story, or during the story if you are smart you get to play online challenges. The good old vendetta from SoM is back. (where you avenge another players death by killing his killer) but now also the online conquer mode, where you conquer another players fort is here. This is incredibly fun, AND it makes you want your own defences are top tier. You don't actually have PvP, but a player can attack your fort which will be defended by your army there at that time.
+ Loot boxes. OMG in the pro section??? YES! Because you "can" buy them for money, but you get them for free too!! and if you do online vendetta's and/or online conquer missions you will never be without loot boxes! You don't need to spend a single penny in micro transactions, vendetta missions for example are a super good means to get your boxes. inside you'll find orcs scaled to your level, legendary gear to your level, training orders for your orcs etc. Forget all the ♥♥♥♥♥ing and moaning, it's actually very exciting to open these boxes and they are very easy to get. And if you decide to pay for them, they are honestly incredibly cheap. I spent some bucks and still have more then 10.000 gold left after I finished the entire game (untill new content comes). they simply make it faster, otherwise you need to find and recruit enemy orcs whereas now you can buy them.
+Nemesis system. Same as SoM, You got to love it how they remember everything, and in SoW orcs that you killed may also come back with the "cheated death" feature, and orcs may also betray you and ambush you. It's just as awesome as it was in shadow of Mordor, but on steroids!
Verdict:
Totally Game of the Year for me. If there would be more content after the Shadow Wars (end game) like all the expansions that are promised combined with a targetting/camera system or an option to turn off the captain cutscenes this game would be a 9.5/10!
A MUST TRY!

This happened because radroaches spawned inside and started siphoning off all my energy, and mole rats for some reason at higher levels siphon energy extremely fast also. Everything siphons energy when you get above 60 people in your vault. The game just spikes in difficulty when you get to 40 and to 60 people so I think the smart way to play the game would be to just sit on your hands and try and pump up all your characters below 39 people and then play the game afterwards.
Even so, the mechanics are stupid. If someone breaks into your vault and nobody is in a room (which happens it seems 90% of the time they go for an empty room) you have to send people from another area, then they inevitably get there too late and the invader burrows to another room, so eventually all your people are running everywhere and you can't keep track of which character has a good gun to actually fight off this invasion. All the while everyones taking radiation damage and physical damage, and they're siphoning off your energy--which in turn shuts down the majority of your vault buildings. Its great. So then you have to temporarily pull people off of every other duty they were doing when your vault was humming like a swiss watch and put them onto energy production then you have to manage to remember to put everyone back where they were before hand--a near impossible task. Its just an annoyance. A huge annoyance.
Then if you're "lucky" you spend the rest of the time just clicking on status updates, like gathering energy, or gathering food, or the rare opportunity that you are able to to level someones stats up. I think this game would be a lot better if the endurance stat did not exist. Apparently the only way to really level up your heroes health a lot is to pump up their endurance. So you have to put all your low levels on endurance training for like 4 real time days to pump up their endurance. Only then can you really make use of them in other capacities if you really want to maximize their experience.
It's pretty dumb. The whole game feels like a waste of time sadly. I just don't have much else to play so I am doing it. I swear though, the first time someone comes in and wipes my vault I am done with this game forever.
Its really a micro transaction game about gambling with the lunchboxes they give you early on. Because lunchboxes (that you have to buy with real money to get in any regularity) contain cards which can help you when you are struggling. But they can also just give you useless legendary materials that 99% of people will never be able to use because they'll quit the game before they can make the stuff. Its stupid. Even then manufacturing a rare weapon took ~16 real hours. I can only imagine a legendary one would take 5 days or something,
So in short. Stay away. It just is not fun enough over the long term...the only real fun I have is going out on quests and even those require you to wait hours and hours unless you buy some nuka cola (yes, real money again) to speed things up. It's just a way to siphon money and its too nakedly obvious to want to even do it. Generally games like this have you provide you with a fun experience along the way, but this one just feels 100% designed to siphon money.

Dustforce truly is a work of art. I don't mean that lightly. The way it's animated plus its music gives it that title in my book. I can find myself playing one level for an hour, maybe even hours at a time. The frustration of losing levels is filled with relaxation and calmness because of the ambient music. The way the levels are crafted is truly mindblowing. They had a system in which you had to perfect a level to earn a key, and you would use that key to earn more levels. In layman's terms, to earn more levels, you had to perfect current levels. They ditched that and added an XP system in which you gain more XP to earn a key the more levels you play and perfect. I'm very glad they added this system and was skeptical about buying it. But now that I did buy it, I do not regret it even for a second. One thing I really love about this game is how you don't have to unlock base levels. In a sense, this game is open world. That sense is that many levels are available to you, and you can choose whether you want to advance into more challenging levels, or stay where you're at. To get an S in completion, you have to sweep up EVERY leaf, and to get an S in Finesse, you have to maintain your combo throughout an entire level.
Another thing I absolutely enjoy about Dustforce is its expasive community. There are lots of Community Workshop maps for you to sharpen your skills on, and lots of people who can set a good example. I'm sure most of the people who get best times on all the levels have a Youtube channel, so you can probably catch them there. The community may or not be active, but it sure is good and friendly.
Overall, in terms of gameplay, music, artstyle, animation, and difficulty (it's not an easy game, but it's not that hard of a game either. It just depends on how much you want to play it), I rate this game:
10/10

Overall I recommend everyone pick this up if you are fan of puzzle games. It contains a high amount of polish and should give you a good 10 hours or so of gameplay. There are some flaws, but I found it to a challenging and fun experience. I think it works well to play it in small periods and take breaks so you do not get too frustrated.
Pros:
Graphics: Beautiful hand painted game. Each area and character looks distinct. Since they are all painted, the game will probably still look good years from now.
Sound: Fully orchestrated score and high quality voice acting. The personality of the charcters come alive through their dialogue. The investments and time they spent on the music and voice acting really pays off, especially with the main characters.
Gameplay: Game is point and click and functions with a vareity of controller options including touch screen. The standard game play is to travel to different areas and solve puzzles to further the game's plot. The puzzles start off fairly easy and progress in difficulty towards the end of the game. Most are fairly fun and can be solved by following established mechanics or using information from items/characters. A few near the end can frustate you, but even then the game tries to give you hints for these. So if you get annoyed, take a break and clear your head. There are some fun chemistry puzzles and ones that use SAT question like logic and even one that involve tree jokes. Near the end, I needed to take pictures of some of the clues, so have your phone or paper handy.
Story: The story is fairly straightfoward and a bit flawed, but the characters and dialogue really shine. Vella is one of the best female protagonist I have seen in a game for a long time. Shay shows some nice growth throughout the game and brings a nice opposing view to the world compared to Vella. All the side characters are are fun to talk to and will make you laugh. In fact every side character feels unique and memorable. Some highlights for me include the tree , the space weaver, and vella's family.
Cons:
Gameplay: The puzzles are interesting, and the game tries to give you hints, but it can be inconsistent about it. One of the aspects I did not like is that its not always obvious when you cannot yet complete a task/puzzle. Some puzzles require other ones to be completed first before you can solve them. The game is not great in explaining this always, so you can feel like stuck and frustrated when trying to solve a puzzle when you simply need some item from another puzzle first. So dont focus too much on anyone puzzle, try switching characters and tasks from time to time. Some puzzles are great at giving you hints and even teleporting you where you need to go if you mess up, but others seem to only clue you in once. Stacking had a nice hint system that might be helpful in this game. I think several big site reviews are frustrated by the boot, knot, and wire puzzles. The wire one is probably the most challenging though the game does try to give you some hints.
Graphics: There not many new areas in Act 2. Most of the places you visited in Act 1 you will see again in Act 2, but through a differing perspective. There are a few new places, but do not expect a lot of new art. All of the characters have new dialogue at least.
Story: The story does not feel entirely complete. On the surface it works and is satisfying enough, but the game definitely leaves a lot of questions about the world and its history. The characters go through their arcs and complete their goals, but there is a lot left for the player to fill in.  It definitely feels like changes were made or story was cut for the sake of time/money. The final puzzle is fun to solve, but from a story perspective, it feels like the motivations could have been better explained.

It’s great to see that Double Fine’s Kickstarter wasn’t a complete flop.
There was a lot of anger towards this game for various reasons of which I do actually understand. The kickstarter was launched asking for $400,000 and they ended up with $3.45 million. Yet they blew their money too quickly and ended up having to release a first act to try and raise funds for the second. Which a lot of people deemed the second act to be lazy and rushed.
All of that aside, in my opinion Double Fine do great games. I’ve been following them for a while now and so far I haven’t been all that disappointed with anything that they’ve made that I have played. Despite their games always having a somewhat childlike feel to them, I always enjoy them.
Sometimes I do wonder if this would have gotten so much hate if the game was released as normal with people being pretty unaware of the recent drama and goings on of Double Fine. If you were to buy this game without knowing anything about it, I think more people would enjoy it.
This was kickstarted shortly after the “Amnesia Fortnight” events that Double Fine did, of which I loved. So I backed this since the beginning. From what feels like forever ago, I just never really bothered all that much actually watching or getting involved with it. It’s kind of been just a dusty book on the shelf until now. I finally got around to playing it and can say I think they did a really great job with it. I may actually go and watch the documentary now.
The story is definitely interesting. Luckily by the time I played it the second act was already out. I can’t imagine myself being all that happy about having to wait quite a while for the next act. But that’s down to pure impatience. I wanted to know what was going on straight away. I was expecting something a little different when it came to the story, but it surprised me in a good way. The story comes together in ways I couldn’t predict.
I think most people’s problem with the story is that a lot of act 1 is the set up. It asks all the questions, it gets you interested and it leaves you on a cliff hanger. After all that waiting, act 2 came out and honestly I can understand people’s disappointment. Most questions are straight up just answered. No real build up. The answers were somewhat brief, vague and honestly there are some holes in the story which made me wonder. I get the feeling most people yearned for more information or something much deeper then what it turned out to be. But I see this game again as almost child-like and light hearted. It honestly didn’t bother me all that much. I still enjoyed it and didn’t at all feel any sense of real disappointment concerning the plot.
The art in the game is really nice. It’s smooth and wonderfully drawn. The audio is well done both music and voice acting wise. I can only assume they blew most of that budget getting Elijah Wood in. The puzzles are straight forward most of the time, which again I think rustled some jimmies. But I honestly enjoyed a little bit more simplicity. It helped the game flow a bit better for me. I could progress and find out what the fudge was going on (I can be impatient when it comes to plotlines). The main kind of puzzle at the end I found a lot of fun. As to where to find the solution is annoying, but deciphering what everything means was quite fun for me.
Usually I end up getting frustrated with point and click games (I think many people do) as it can sometimes be pretty easy to get stuck.
Admittedly, I still got stuck on this a few times for a fair while but the puzzles and combinations are logical enough to not be stuck (and therefore annoyed) for very long. It’s also a nice feature to the game being able to switch between characters and take a break from what you were doing.
The annoying part is the achievements (if you are even into achievements, I suppose). I personally insisted on 100%ing the game.
It took me 18 hours and I have to say it was a little tedious. That may be just because I stayed up until 1am no-lifing and ended up quite tired and annoyed with it… but still. If you’re looking for an easy 100% it’s not all that easy. It’s do-able but you’ll need to be meticulous, complete it a few times over and be able to be quite fast about a complete play through to do it.
All in all, I enjoyed this game. I thought it was great. Was also nice to see Pendleton Ward doing some voice work for Double Fine after the last Amnesia Fortnight. I hope to see more of that.
Keep it up Double Fine!
TL;DR : Despite all the recent Double Fine drama, it’s a great story,  it had good audio, visuals and puzzles. It has achievements that actually do feel an achievement to get and it just generally is another great game by Double Fine. I’d think any point and click or Double Fine fan would like this game. If you’re neither or those things, try it anyway. I still think there’s a chance you might enjoy it despite Double Fine’s games always having a slight childlike feel to them.

Broken Age mixes a wonderful story of two perfect strangers chosen to fulfill a great destiny with beautiful hand-painted aesthetics to create one of the best graphic adventures of all time.
Divided in two acts (one which came out February 2014, the other April 2015) you control both characters in different environments, having the ability to switch between them at any given time. Sometimes, the actions from one affect the other, which makes some of the puzzles hard and compelling.
The story itself is amazing, one the best I've ever seen. Combining sci-fi with fantasy, finally creating one of the best atmospheres you could imagine for this kind of game.
Totally recommended.

There are no perks, which was one of my favorite things about the old Fallouts. Lots of bad UI and design features seem to be carried over for no reason other than to make it slightly more similar to old Fallout, which were fine in 1999 but kinda painful now.

This game is quite honestly tough to rate as it will make you feel conflicted. Nonetheless, here is my take on this game.
Please note that some positives also pave the way to a negative that you will see below.
Positives
- Increased map size. Now divided into regions. Each is about the size of one of the two sections in SOM.
- New abilities. From leaping off your enemies, chaining stealth kills, and even chaining shadow strike kills. There are more but I am trying to keep this review spoiler clean.
- New missions for followers(From hunting catagors, graug, to even raiding captains supplies).
- Story, the missions were engaging and kept me playing. The game's cutscenes were well done in my opinion.
- Combat has been improved, however it does take getting use to and has negatives.
- Some abilities will consume focus instead of your arrows(elf-shot). You can increase your amount of focus by equipping better gear.
Cons
- Abilities, while listed as a positive because it brings something new to the table, the way in which it was done makes you scratch your head and questions what was going through the developers heads. There are core abilities and then modifiers for said abilities. Ex. Shadow strike is a base abilitiy with three modifiers. But, and here is the negitive, you can either choose one of those three options, two off my head are, chaining your attacks to other enemies near you, or being able to target an enemy and dominate them instantly. In addition if you want to dominate basic enemies you must have that modifier enabled. Due to this change it feels as though you have to miss out on certain play styles as what was once basic, is now something you have to choose to have because instead of dominating basic enemies you can have it to where it would replenish your arrows( or elf- shot). Not using this will cause you quite often to have no arrows to use on a captain that can only be damaged by range or stealth... in a fortress.
- Repetitive enemies. One new type of enemy is introduced... that's it. Ologs. Bigger and attacks cannot be countered. Enemies often look the same despite cosmetics on their appearance having variety. You will feel as though you are fighting the same enemy over and over again. The nemesis engine attempts to solve this problem with adding personalities. While it does add depth to the combat system with captains able to adapt to your moves if used to much, you still see personalities being repeated, though there are a greater amount of them.
- Travel. By travel, I mean being able to get around. Talion's basic run speed is extremely slow. Feels as though you are simply crawling and the fast travel points are often far from your destination/follower mission.
- Story. Multiple times I could tell what was going to happen long before it did.
- Missions for your followers can be repetitive. When attempting to level up one follower, I ended up doing 3-4 of the same mission in a row while also having to travel back and forth across the map to them, becoming quite tedious.
- Micro-transactions. While I did not experience too invasive ads, I did not do any multiplayer sieges. However, the game is priced at $60 USD, micro-transactions are priced at 100 maximum for an amount of 10k gold with 2k bonus. Cost of some of the items is 860 gold for a bundle of three chests. woohoo. I did not spend any money and instead used the currency that is available to be earned in-game for completing the story and optional objectives.
This game feels more like a study of what we gamers will accept as a new normal. If you feel as though you must get this game, do not encourage further additions of Micro-transactions in games by using them and spending more money. I cannot recommend this game.

I cannot recommend this game at this price. Which is a shame because I *really* wanted to give this game every chance. I heard the complaints of the console players (I had friends who traded the disc back in after three days - it was that bad), and waited two and a half months for the PC version to come out (with patches) so I could give it a go.
What I've experienced so far has confirmed the bad news. This just isn't a very good game, unfortunately.
NEGATIVES:
- Gameplay is clunky, rigid, and incredibly repetitive (especially in career mode).
- Like previous titles, the gameplay is just kick, mark, tackle, kick, mark, tackle... with the odd free kick here and there.
- The difficulty jump from easy to medium is insane. On easy with 5 minute quarters, I win by 10+ goals with ease. On medium, I'm lucky to even score anything.
- Graphics, while not important, are lacklustre here.
- Commentary is great for the first five minutes, after which you will hear the same thing over and over. Richardson's fake inspirational dribble at the beginning of every quarter is incredibly cringey.
- No drills/controls advice in free roam. You have to search through the controls menu yourself to learn how to play the game.
POSITIVES:
- The facescanned players look fantastic on the players hub. Though why did they bother scanning every player if they only used the results on the 5-6 star players of each team?
- The stadiums look pretty nice, I played a twilight game at Metricon Stadium and the sunset effect was glorious.
- The Bont is on the front cover.
I know this game was made on a low budget. I know that an AFL game can never ever reach the levels of a FIFA or NBA game. I know the sport itself is tricky to translate into a video game. But what is on offer here is just not good enough. If this is the best they can manage after so long, then I really doubt we'll ever see a good quality AFL video game.
Save your money. Pick it up if it ever goes on sale if you're absolutely desperate.

Alan Wake is a third person adventure game about a writer trying to save his wife and at the same time decide if he's going crazy. But is this really a game, or more like an slightly interactive story? Let's find out.
My impression about Alan Wake is that it is a game made not by game designers but TV screenwriters. The game has an episodic structure, with an ending song for each one and a recap at the beginning of the next. The game draws inspiration from mystery and horror novels and movies, but the setting is clearly inspired by nineties TV series Twin Peaks, to a point that the game is almost a tribute to it. The idea of the small village in the woods where everything is darker than it seems. The lady of the light versus the log lady. C'mon, man, even the diner resembles the Double R.
Apart from the setting, the game relies heavily on its story. You can argue about is originality, but overall Alan Wake has a surprisingly good storytelling, at least  compared to videogame standards. Maybe the only flaw is that the tone is a little inconsistent. Sometimes only hints of what's happening are revealed to the player (as it should be on this kind of story, in my opinion), and sometimes you are explained everything like if you were a kid.
Let's talk now about the gameplay. Unfortunately, this aspect of the game is not as deep as we can expect. Most of the levels consist on running to something or running from something, generally through the forest at night. As a shooter, the game is really oversimplified, and while the lightning mechanic is interesting, it looses the sense of doing something new after a couple hours. There are at least some vehicle levels, but overall the gameplay is quite monotone.
The graphics are pretty good for the age of the game. I played it recently on a TV and they scale quite well. The art direction is not really outstanding but it does its job, it sets the dark / mystery atmosphere Alan Wake needs, so no complaints on this point. The audio is great, mainly because of the great soundtrack of the game, combining existing songs with some specifically written for the game.
So, what you need to know to decide if you should buy? If you are looking for a good story that keep you entertained for about ten hours, but don't mind a gameplay experience that is too simple, go for it, you'll enjoy it. If you want more gameplay depth, this is not for you.

If you are new to paladins or have been considering downloading the game, here is my warning: The game is becoming pay to win. The new card system allows players to pay, to max out the stats on every card n the game allowing them to make an overpowered loadout.
The old card system was fine. It allowed any player to unlock any card and customize their loadout. Everyone was still able to play well without an amazing loadout. We were allowed to freely choose how good to make certain cards. Now all of my loadouts are gone, and replaced with 3 random loadouts for each champion that I cannot get rid of. Adding the new card system was a terrible mistake by Hi-Rez. They could have spent their time fixing bugs instead of adding a  pay to win system that a lot of players dislike.
Not only that, older players like me were not reimbursed wih the new champion chests for each champion, that you get after every level up (the champion chests level up your cards for just that specific champion). For example my level 16 drogoz does not get to have any of the 16 champion chests that would have been unlocked.
I dont understand what Hi-Rez was thinking after the community saying they disliked this system.  I have invested time and money into this game just to watch it go to♥♥♥♥♥♥ The game is extremely unbalanced now, with level 4 loaodout players vs level 10 loadout players. This game used to take skill, not money to succeed. Dont get me wrong, I love this game, my review prior to this was good. This game gave me hours of fun. The game is now getting progressively worse and not better, and it makes me sad. I am hoping that this review doesnt stay for long. I would love to somehow see this disaster fixed.
All in all, if you want to play an unbalanced game where you need to either spend money or grind for hours on end to be equal to the players who pay, then you will enjoy this game.

I would not classify this as the "poor man's Overwatch," although I see the blantant similarities, just as Overwatch is similar to TF2;  Paladins mixes more MOBA elements with the class-based shooter aesthetic popularized in Team Fortress 2.
With the addition of Legendary cards, which greatly amplifies a single ability or attack of a character, it has other cards that do similar effects to the chararcter, like reduces Cooldown on a paticular ability or increases base health for a deployable or improved base health.   Additionally, each character can be visually customized with mix and matching of cosmetics.
These customizations options are a double edged sword for the player, as both the cards and cosmetics are Hi-Rez's form of monetization, besides thier founder's pack which unlocks all the characters.   The exclusives through chests just feels bad as  player, similar to Smite.  SInce this is still in Beta many of the cosmetics are limited and most are just recolors (some are very meh or even poorly done).
Maps are semi-varied, but overall pretty similar.  All are pretty much outdoor with the same aestethic of mossy ruins or icy ruins.  I like the character design, but issues with gameplay balancing only made worse with introduction of legendary cards.
Pros:
+Good Gameplay
+Varied Character Design with okay customization
+Decent alternative to Overwatch despite many differences
Cons:
-HiRez trying too hard to monetize (Chests, Legendary Cards/Essence System, dependence on Boosts),
or doesn't feel like i get enough bang for my buck
-Major character balancing issues patch to patch (even if in beta)
-Lots of crashes (some to the EasyAntiCheat)
I think it's worth a try.  I still feel like Hi-Rez tries to overmonitize thier games, but they are still fun due to low cost.

Hard to say whether I recommend or not.  Game is definitely hit and miss, unfortunately so.
The story, characters, voice acting, cutscenes and music are all amazing and give the setting a very genuine feel.
There has been many graphical glitches haven't seen many gameplay glitches except an enemy getting stuck in a wall.  The way cars peel out and move feels very convincing (when using realistic mode especially) however car damage and physics leave ALOT to be desired.  Alot of cars you hit are sent flying over you as if you were in a tank and many times you will hit a vehicle and either no or inconsistent damage will be done to you or it.
My biggest problem so far is the repetitiveness of the missions.  Also how dumb the AI is.  You have to be pretty wreckless or bad to find this game difficult at all even on hard.  Granted this type of game isnt about the challenge but at least give those that want it that option.  The missions are pretty samey throughout so far and it just makes you wonder what the hell goes on behind the scenese at dev studios now days.  Like how can a group of smart, experienced programers and gamers collabratively come together over 4 years and provide us with somethinng so repetitive doing a complete disservice to the wonderful characters and settiing they created.
Furthermore, the game is basically void of extra activites, character progression and customization.  Cannot even change your clothes or get a haircut.  You cannot walk into a store and purchase anything so dont be fooled when watching videos and you see bars and diners on players' maps.  You can only real walk in and take the money and walk out.
You also never really feel like a boss.  Your "underbosses" send you on petty missions that their henchmen should be doing and you never get to tell people what to do and deal with mob politics.  So many missed opportunites in this game.  Hopefully devs take notice of players' criticisms and add these features through DLC (many of which being free), it would be such a tradegy to let this rich on an era and this great setting, music and characters go to waste.
After typing this, I would have to say I cannot in good faith recommend this game to others after seeing my thoughts on it written down.  I hope that changes in the future.

I played the original in 1988 as a 12 year old and was throughly drawn into the game, playing it to completion several times.  It was like playing Fallout 10 years before everyone else.  When Fallout came out, I was excited sure enough it lived up to the type of gaming the original Wasteland put out.  That said, even though the world has moved on to 3D, I was really excited to see Wasteland 2 being made.  I did wait a few months to play it after it released, to let the bugs and rough edges iron out and I'm glad I did.  It is a pretty fantastic game that lives up to the original as well as the fallout games that came after that.
Graphics being what they were in 1988, Wasteland 2 is like getting to play that game as my imagination augmented the original as I played it.  The writing has the same gritty, hard faced attitude that the original game did and many of the same life and death consequences for your actions.  What it lacks in 3D it makes up for with descriptive text that gives it that old school feel and the need to use skills to get special items.  This is not a console game that will hold your hand and let you operate it on two buttons and a joypad.  This game is dark, challenging, will test your patience and wits and you will need a notebook to get the most out of it.  Yes, you need to write down names, connections, clues, maybe location of that treasure you had to walk past because you couldn't blow open the door blocking your way to it.  Life and death choices will be made.  You may have to stand by and watch raiders execute innocent people because you are not strong enough to fight them yet.  You might take the wrong door have to kill more people than you wanted to achieve a goal.  I remember in the 1988 game, finding a howizer and some shells near a town.  I had fun firing it, the glee of firing the big gun and the holes it was leaving in ground.  Then I remember the horror when I found that one of the shells had come down in town and killed the cute girl who ran the hobo dog stand.  You'll face this kind of thing in Wasteland 2 as well.
Then there is the AI.  The AI has no qualms about planting a knuckle out punch right into your kidney.  I found a way around a guarded gate and set up behind a crate thinking, "hahaha... I'll be cheap and make them come around and face my firing squad here."  The game AI would have none of that.  Instead the bad guys repositioned themselves around cover in an ambush stance and made me come out to them.  Ouch!  I prevailed, but I paid in a lot of pain for my win.  It seems that the combat AI was very thoughly thought through.
So if you like gritty, sun burnt style gaming with well written descriptions to go with the visuals and none of the candy coating you seem to often get in some of todays games, you'll probably enjoy this one.  The bad news is there are a few rough edges, clicking on the map doens't move you.  No fast exit from a place you've been.  No map zoom. A few dialog bugs and even trigger glitches.   But these are minor things and I've found the team will listen to these kind of concerns via twitter and other social media and at least add them to the list of considerations for future updates.  So if you play and find something you don't like, reach out on facebook or twitter and make yourself heard.  The publisher will at least listen if not possibly act.

How did one of the most successful Kickstarter campaigns of all time turn into this shlop? I am a slow paced gamer. I like to waddle around and smell the pixels. I appreciate the acrylic backgrounds and beautifully voiced characters. This game may be categorized under "puzzle games," but if you play it for the puzzles, you would be far more entertained by Freddie Fish. Rather, this is more like a beautiful children's book about the perils of being a teenager and growing into adulthood-something all of us can relate to (Except bronies. Boom! Shots fired!). Yet, it failed miserably to live up to its potential. Rather than dwelling into the complexities of human emotion, the plotline fell apart like cottage cheese. The player was sent around doing meaningless tasks that did not in any shape, way, or form contribute to either the story or character development. Hastily built plothole bandaids were dumped like so much dog s*** onto the unsuspecting player. Every character's personality was rendered in glorious 2-D. Nobody was the least bit affected by the traumatization that they experienced. No explanation was given concerning the constant breaches of the fourth wall made by the omnipresent player. Needless to say, this was painful to play. My hopes have been dashed, and I am beyond disappointed with how long I waited for this game.

The game is also difficult enough that I don't feel bad about savescumming. At first I was honestly wondering why there wasn't an ironman mode because that seems to be so popular nowadays, but I see why. I can't in good conscious recommend Wasteland 2 as a finished product. It's too lackluster and has a few major issues. It plays fine, and I will probably continue playing it even after I write this, but there's two main issues at the time of writing.
The first being off is the god for saken prison. Ran by raiders with no redeemable factors that turn people into slaves only be disguising them as workers. They do nothing good, everyone that you come across will say you can be the savior, march right up to the leader, and kill him, simple task, right?
Apparently not, once you get there you run into a plotwall. Two turrets at 4K health each(To put that in perspective, 20ish hours in my characters only have 125ish health). Okay, fine, just bring out heavy weapons. Wrong again, they have a stupid high intiative, and a stupid high amount of action points. They fired 5ish times each, doing 300 damage per bullet. Good luck getting your party through that.
Even if you *DO* manage to kill the turrets, there's apparently accounts of impossible-to-defuse landmines that 1 hit kill party members.
Why is this happening? I'm not sure, but if I had to guess, one of the team members working on wasteland felt so proud of their plot twist they decided to make sure everyone can only expirence the plot twist like that. So you just have to go 'welp, i know these guys beat and enslave you, but hes's got deus ex machina backing him so we can't do anything till the game says so'
The other issue is just hour 10ish. It becomes out-of-ammo gun-jam simulator. You won't have enough ammo to get into skrims, or if you do, you'll be cutting it close and it'll just be fustrating. Then when you do have ammo, your gun jams. A lot. I'm not sure how complex a double barrel shotgun is, but i'm pretty sure it's not prone to the amount of jamming it got.
Now for the nitpicky stuff. Somethings just outpace your levels, but that's fine, maybe I shouldn't be rushing through the content as fast as I was. Another issue is just not being able to interact with the world. There's a girl who's (perpetually) dying, constantly groaning into your radio, asking for some one named Elroy. You can find her, confront her. But even if you're the best doc of the entire world, you can't help her, only shoot her. It may sound super nit picky, but not even given the illusion of choice sucks. I couldn't try, I could only mercy kill.
There is good htngs, the game is close to being a perfect masterpiece.
Combat is actually alright, atleast mid game. Things start getting faster, combat is quick but a bit tactical. It could benefit from a few small tweaks. Flanking, some more cover options, and a change to friendly fire calculations(Not as bad as fallout 2. Damn it Sulik, give me that gun.)
The characters are alright, followers feel human as they comment on the scenery and situation where applicable, instead of being a silent moving turret. They have their flaws, they have their benefit, but not so much so they become a god send or dead weight.
Over all the game feels... unpolished. It feels as if I'm playing in a beta, which I'm not. If it gets changed, or the mod tools get released, I'm sure this game could be something fantastic. But at the moment it's simply okay.

I kickstarted Broken Age back when it was called Double Fine Adventure, and comming in my expectation was to get something that played as well as the Lucas Arts games of old, with large worlds to explore, a lot of things to interact with, and puzzles that make me feel proud about figuring them out (or stupid for not doing so when I finally get it).
When I got to play the first episode the first thing i reacted to was the art style. The game really has a picture book for kids vibe that continues through the entire game. If you can stand it, the graphics are pretty, and the animations are smooth. I thought the game was over all pretty, but it's up to your taste if you can stand it.
The voices are also well done. All character have well sounding voices, and what little dialogue there is is mostly well written, and some characters are memorable and likable. What little plot there is is interesting, and in the end I must concede that Double Fine managed to create an interesting world I would like to return to in what will hopefully be a Broken Age 2.
All that said, why is this a negative review? Well, the game has very little content when it comes to gameplay.
Over all there are very few objects you can carry around, and mostly it is fairly obvious what they are supposed to be used for. This means that the item based puzzles are trivial to solve.
Act 1 mostly consists of moving around in the cloud kingdom and a fishing village for Vella, and a space ship for Shay. The puzzles are mostly embarassingly easy fetch quests, and to be fair, act 1 might make a good introduction to adventure games for a young child. Act 1 ends with a plot twist I enjoyed, and after it I was looking forward to the meat of the game that I thought would be act 2.
Act 2 mostly consists of moving around in the cloud kingdom and fishing village as Shay, and a space ship for Vella.
The puzzles are still mostly embarassingly easy fetch quests, there are a few mildly tricky puzzles, and then there are a few puzzles that are just a big slap in the face where the solution is only obvious after you have solved it, or only available to the other character as something they might comment on or see in the background.
The end game mostly centers around wiring up robots with patterns only the other character can find, and the ending really didn't feel very satisfactory to me, but it does leave room for a sequel which I hope we will get to see.
The main problem with act 2 is that it doesn't really expand on act 1. The characters are still stuck in the same small world with only a few items and the same characters as in act 1 available to them to use at any time, and ultimately that leaves the puzzles no more interesting than the ones in the introduction that is act 1. Ultimately I have to ask: What took so long? After years of development I was expecting a lot more gameplay content than this.
Broken age is not a bad game, but it is not a very good one either. I'd give it a neutral grade if I could. I don't hate it, but why waste time on it when you could be playing something better?

I was a huge fan of the previous version, Shadow of Mordor and this version took it to the next level. It was improved on every single aspect so I totally recommend it. Not only to fans of the previous version, but also for people that never played the series. The story stands on itself, you won't miss much, but it deffinitely helps if you played the first, The story goes on where Shadow of Mordor ended.
All this being said, with new content and goodies also came new irritations. So I still recommend it to everyone, but there are certainly things that could have been done much better. Lets take a look at the pro's and con's.
-Camera! Seriously it is the most annoying part of this game. 70% of the time the 3rd person camera is fine, but in 30% of the times you'll be adjusting it with your right stick just to see where you want to go. This is infuriating after the third time you die because your camera was pointing in the completely wrong direction. This should be fixes ASAP in an update.
-Sometimes, thanks to the nemesis system a boss becomes almost unbeatable on your own. Especially the bosses with the No Chance perk (you don't get to have the option to deflect the final blow) are VERY hard in certain circumstances and when they are high level. If you take into consideration some bosses have caragors, spear throwers and berserkers with them while they on themselves also have accumulated strong defences and can kill you with 3 blows it can be very hard to beat them. It took me a while to figure out you have another option to kill your arch enemy and that is by sending 1-3 of your own captains to kill him. You can assist if you want. But before I figured this out, it was very hard and often irritating.
-Once you reach chpt 4, the game is much easier/faster if you invested in Loot boxes. It's a simple fact. If you bought your orcs, it will be faster to have strong up to par captains for the challenge at hand. (but that's it, I'll come back to loot boxes in the pro section!)
-In Shadow of Mordor, every time you got a skill point, you became stronger either way. In shadow of War you must chose your build. This means if you get a skill point you can invest it in 1 main power, which has then 2-3 sub posers. But unlike SoM you need to choose ONE of the subpowers, so you can't have them all. For some that may be intruiging, but I miss the feeling of becoming all powerfull like you had in SoM. In Shadow of War you'll sometimes change your subpowers to meet the challenge in front of you (like a nemessis with very specific defences). I simply find that annoying and wish it was like SoM: every skill point accumulates your strength.Additionally, if you complete the game you have surplus skill points that you can't spend (yet) which imho is poor logic, as now we have a constant reminder we have unspent skill points, but we can't spend them...
-I'll combine my final two irritations: Cut scenes and targetting. Every time a captain enters the fray, a cutscene starts his introduction. This is in the midlle of the fight, where the camera turns towards him, and stays on him after the intro. This was awesome in SoM, but in SoW you will face many captains at the same time, many times! Now without a targetting system (Come ON, this can not be hard to implement!!!) you will constantly lose focus on the boss you where fighting. You will also die because of this or captains will manage to escape because of this, and your own captains will die during sieges because of this. A targetting system that holds your boss during cut scenes) would solve all this instantly... This is without a doubt the real negative in this game.
Now the pro's!
+ Story. Excellent addition to SoM story and for example the movies. Especially the story of Shelob got me intruiged. Very well done again and I can't wait for the DLC stories! Only downside: it was a bit short, they tried to dragg it along with the 10 stage shadow wars, but take those away and it's pretty short.
+ Orc duels. A very cool addition is to have your orcs fight vs enemy orcs in the arena. Especially since you can train your own orcs to a certain degree. I honestly had a lot of fun cheering for my favorite hand made Olog fighting other captains! (You can't intervene a duel, so all you can do is spectate)
+ Training your orcs. You can train your orcs by giving them missions so they level up, or by using loot boxes that contain training orders. So you can give your captains caragors, fire weapons, resistance to cetain dmg etc... It's a very cool addition especially combined to the duels in the arenas.
+ new skills like double jump, shadow dominate, ressurect fallen enemies/friends are all very nice.
+ Gear. You can collect and level legendary gear. It's a nice addition and it makes you want to collect the entire set. Upgrading gear is done by doing a certain mission, like dominate an orc from the marauder tribe, higher then lvl 30-40-55-60. And you want a full set for the extra bonusses so it's additional content, that makes you stronger.
+ Once you finished the story, or during the story if you are smart you get to play online challenges. The good old vendetta from SoM is back. (where you avenge another players death by killing his killer) but now also the online conquer mode, where you conquer another players fort is here. This is incredibly fun, AND it makes you want your own defences are top tier. You don't actually have PvP, but a player can attack your fort which will be defended by your army there at that time.
+ Loot boxes. OMG in the pro section??? YES! Because you "can" buy them for money, but you get them for free too!! and if you do online vendetta's and/or online conquer missions you will never be without loot boxes! You don't need to spend a single penny in micro transactions, vendetta missions for example are a super good means to get your boxes. inside you'll find orcs scaled to your level, legendary gear to your level, training orders for your orcs etc. Forget all the ♥♥♥♥♥ing and moaning, it's actually very exciting to open these boxes and they are very easy to get. And if you decide to pay for them, they are honestly incredibly cheap. I spent some bucks and still have more then 10.000 gold left after I finished the entire game (untill new content comes). they simply make it faster, otherwise you need to find and recruit enemy orcs whereas now you can buy them.
+Nemesis system. Same as SoM, You got to love it how they remember everything, and in SoW orcs that you killed may also come back with the "cheated death" feature, and orcs may also betray you and ambush you. It's just as awesome as it was in shadow of Mordor, but on steroids!
Verdict:
Totally Game of the Year for me. If there would be more content after the Shadow Wars (end game) like all the expansions that are promised combined with a targetting/camera system or an option to turn off the captain cutscenes this game would be a 9.5/10!
A MUST TRY!
