M-E: Shadow of War... That indeed is a title to any nerd and/or geek that has read Tolkiens books, so instantly you have high hopes and expectations for the title.. In my case its more or less "
."
I'll try to keep this review short but with a valid and simple core to help you understand why
haven't enjoyed this game too much.
For me games should be an adventure, you know, depth, pace, experience, twists, surprises and this game for the most  part was. Really good story, first 20-30 hours were well paced with side guests and collectables, this game had 110% of my attention in every bit of the story and collectibles, every single alphabeth in every word. It was amazing to try and find each and every bit of the story to understand more of this world... But thats mostly all the game really offered me personally.
As a gamer that has played, reviewed and experienced hundreds games and tens to hundreds of thousands of hours of different gameplay, the skilltrees were a mess. Anyone who knows how to screw around, have fun but still be efficient orc slaying machine would know that 70-80% of the skills and "upgrades" were below "optional". Why go with an ability that increases your might from Stealth kills, that hardly really matters when you have to fight 90% of the game 1.vs.legion, than with an ability that triples your Might generation from successful attacks, that works well with chain executions that you can almost every 4th or 5th attack (2-3 crits, which also comboes well with crit abilities) chain to kill and stack your hit-streak on multiple orcs, instakilling them and giving you an instant edge in the battle? Or you can use that might to insta drain/dominate orcs, or deal different types of aoe dot effects and wiping that army down instantly. I dont understand, it hardly lets you be creative with your builds and playstyles.
Lets talk about gear, which is also a good part of the game... And it bored me. Early Legendaries are boring, leveling them up is like going to the gym... but already exhausted for banging your neighbors daughter. Legendaries a re supposed to be Legendary, tho you seem to find 1 legendary orc after 3 turns... Wheres the "legendary" in that?.. And when you finaly level them up to 60, they are so underwhelming and seen so far into the game... But I gotta say that the set bonuses lets you screw around with possible builds.
And not gonna waste too much on the Orcs. Yeah, some of them are unique...
(♥♥♥♥ing love my Tower orc thats Cursed, boosts other Savages,  is immune to all effects and has tremendous amount of health with a butt loads  of other perks, and is not even Legendary, but Epic <_> )
...But leveling them up, "gearing" them up well and correctly, fighting some of them... Its just too grindy even for me.. And I have spent around 10 years on WoW non-stop, which is around 20k hours. I like grinding a lot, some times it satisfying when done well (Warframes combat keeps the grind amazing. WoW's combat and the feeling of success when you finaly get that one Achievement, even tho it doesnt do jack...) I cant say that this game grindfest satisfying at all... Either sitting there for 3 minutes to Pokemon your orcs, or babysitting them on an ambush is just boring, not rewarding...
Combat is also a big meh. Its uncomplicatedly complicated. You press couple of buttons, thats it. Then you face against an orc  that can only be killed with stealth attacks, and there you go running  around the fortress for 40 minutes stealthing him and hoping the ♥♥♥♥er doesn't adapt in time... Or use his weakness and daze him to lay hell upon him... But good luck finding a ♥♥♥♥ing graug in the middle of a fortress...
Its not a bad game, but nowhere close of being a masterpiece. Its just Good, Average, Meh, Good waste of couple of hours waiting for your friends to come Online.

Shadow of War has improved on almost everything from Shadow of Mordor (besides a few bugs) and then ruined it all with their loot boxes.
As you probably know, loot boxes give you weapons, orcs, orc powerups and XP boosts.
You can buy the low level loot boxes with the in game Silver you get, and you get a lot of it. You can also pony up and spend real money on Gold to buy high level loot boxes (you can also get some Gold from daily challenges).
And the result of the loot boxes is that
.
In Shadow of Mordor, the only way to get loot was killing captains. Getting a powerful weapon was an achievement. You would send death threats to the most powerful captains, making them more powerful, learn their weaknesses, then have a really tough fight to beat them. Now I can spend some of my free in game silver money to get a loot box which gives me 2 fairly decent bits of loot. The sense of acheivement is gone completely, there is literally no incentive to kill captains now, its always better to recruit them.
Then there are the orcs. It seems like they have decided to make the game massive and grindy near the end to encourage you to fast track some of that by buying orcs loot boxes. So they made the end of the game super boring and repetitive because of the loot boxes.
The very fact that loot boxes are in a game means they will want to provide incentives to buy them, which results in creating time consuming elements to encourage people to skip them. Its the same as what happened to mobile games, but now we are seeing it in full priced AAA games and it is resulting in a game that is boring as hell in the second part.
I, like other reviewers, haven't finished the game, because it is not fun to play after a certain point.
I loved Shadow of Mordor and prepurchased Shadow of War, and yes I thoroughly enjoyed the short time I have played, but I am sad that loot boxes turned this game from a gem into a turd. I honestly looked forward to this since the first game and I am bitterly disappointed.

The story is the main meat of the game and it is interesting enough for you to keep playing, exploring and solving problems for the people of the wasteland. The quests have several possible solutions and diffrent outcomes; good, bad, partial success and failure states. If the game gets a bit more polish and some mod support it's certainly worth to play again to see some of the other versions of the story.

You know what, I'd love to tell you how great this game is. How wonderful the graphics are, how fluent the controls are... but you know what, I can't. And why? I think it has to with the fact that, oh wait let me think...
I. CAN. NOT. ♥♥♥♥ING. SIGN. IN.
You know, this game has intrigued me, ever since I first heard about it. I looked as if Overwatch and TF2 set aside their differences and had a baby, whose elements were a mix of both. And I thought, "Oh, if it's free to play, why not give it a try."
So I hit download.
How I regret that decision.
After 2 hours and 11 minutes not to mention an additional 10 for all the first time setup biz, I'm at the login screen. I was a little bummed you had to make a separate account but hey, it doesn't matter. I create an account with Google as it's quick and easy; just hit Allow a couple times. I do that and it says, "Connect with your Hi-Rez account." Huh. I thought I just made it. So I hit the create button and WHOOP-DE-DOO I'M BACK AT THE SAME SCREEN I STARTED! Even better, I hit Create with Google and it says in red font, "This account is already in use." So I hit sign-in, and it gives me the username and password screen. Just to clarify, I DIDN'T GET THE OPTION TO CHOOSE EITHER!! So I guess I just have to accept the fact that my email is just lost in the void of your server files, Hi-Rez.
But hey, I wasn't ready to give up so easily. I mean, this is why throwaway and backup emails exist, right? So I decide to make a brand-new, spankin' good looking Hi-Rez account! SCREW THE EASE OF SIGNING IN WITH GOOGLE! THIS IS THE REAL DEAL!! So I fill out EVERY FIELD!! USERNAME, CHECK! PASSWORD, GOT THAT! CONFIRM PASSWORD, GUESS I HAVE TOO! EMAIL,
(not my real email, or any in that case). So every field, hit create, get taken to the splash/news screen and FINALLY HIT PLAY!! At last. I'm in the game. Background music... an options menu... actual hint that the game exists... Sweet tranquility... =w=...
Oh? Fill in my credentials? Well I just did that. Why not fill it in again once more.
Username: Starman45FTW
Password: **********
...
I am at the breaking point. I close out the game and get taken back to the login screen. That red "incorrect login" font TAUNTING me. I give it one last chance. I hit "Can't Login?". I get taken to the "Forget Password" screen on their website in my browser.
This it it. The ultimate failsafe.
I enter my email.
"We have sent your Username to your email"
I am taken to the login screen.
I enter the sorry excuse of a username which is nothing more than a string of letters and numbers.
I enter my alleged password.
...
The red box dominates my screen.
"LOGIN ERROR"
The words resonate with me, scream at me.
Tears well up in my eyes.
I am about to close the window when that one word in the bottom left of that red box catches my eye.
Despite being in all lowercase, the word yells at me louder than any in caps lock.
"failure"
"failure"
0/10. The only failure here, is you, Hi-Rez. Take hint and let players sign in with their Steam.

Garry's Mod. GMod.
A game I wanted when I was younger, since people did silly things in it, such as goofy youtube "animations". I watched some weird sonic series where someone used sonic character rag-dolls.
After having owned the game for some fair amount of time, and playing it with my friends, it's a fairly decent game.
I mean, having said "it's a fairly decent game", I take that back. The game itself is garbage. Fueled by the community workshop, with pretty much everything possible, the game can be made to be something impressive.
It runs on the source, engine... so for the most part, it's really generic, and clunky, and things feel a bit... unstable.
Does this ruin the experience? Heck no! While you won't have much fun directly after installing the game, without adding anything, the game is a sandbox game of sorts where you can make whatever you want from it.
"The game itself is garbage", if you are referring to the actual base game itself.
It's not designed to be anything special though, it's a simple formula.
Definitely worth the ~£5 imo, me and my friends shared a lot of laughter while playing on this, and I hope that you do too.
So yeah, overall, GMod is great and you should definitely give it a try.

Just finished the complete game, including my 3rd play through the first "Act", and I have to say I definitely felt I got a $10 million experience—Double Fine put in the time, effort, and funds, and it paid off. Beautiful artwork, fun & interesting characters, quirky settings, and the layers within layers of "twists" in the plot were fun even though they were pretty obvious [to me].
With the full game in perspective, the "half" formerly known as "Act I" feels more like a prologue; it teaches you the interface, introduces the characters, setting, and plot, and it isn't until you reach "Act II" that the game really seems to begin. The game wouldn't work at all without the first act, but its value doesn't really become clear until you reach the second.
Having recently played through some "classic" adventure games (e.g.: Monkey Island 1 & 2), I am grateful for the advancements of modern gaming & interface (thank goodness verbs are gone!) design, while still challenged by some of the puzzles and sometimes-tiny-and-obscure clues. In my opinion, Double Fine is taking adventure games in the right direction and, with all the time & effort they've invested in the engine, I look forward to seeing more adventure games from them in coming years.

Natural Selection 2 is everything that makes a shooter great. Never before have I seen an asymmetric shooter that has so much love to detail and balance. It has good variety in weapons and "enemies" while making sure there is no such thing as useless equipment. Everything has a use and is viable, be it the starting rifle, the side pistol or the first alien life form.
This game promotes and, indeed, needs team play and communication. An absolute fantastic online experience best enjoyed in 7v7 or 8v8 matches so to not lose the tactical feel as well as the importance of every individual involved.
However, it is important to say that this game has an incredibly steep learning curve and will take several hours to even get your head around. Especially the role of the commander should not be taken before completely understandly the flow and priorities of matches as well as tactics. I myself have not filled the com station until 40 hours into the game for it is the most stressful and important position in every match. The community is very much aware of this learn curve and is, in general, very eager to explain the many questions beginners might have. And don't shy away from learning the alien side! It is an asymmetric shooter, after all.
I can not recommend this game more appart from the dwindling player base as this game continues to age. It is definately my favorite shooter of all times and I really hope this game will see a continuation even though I would be just as happy with just a revival of the once large player base. Giving it a 10 would not suffice. This game has heavily influenced what I expect of online shooters to come.

Liked:
+ Gun mechanics are enjoyable and satisfying. There's a large enough variety of guns with differing mechanics that gives me that feel that I haven't mastered everything. The audio and visual feedback of shooting and hitting enemies is well done.
+ Mutation variety, married with the character variety, creates many different combinations that encourages exploration and provides additional mechanics to master. Especially when each character has differences that aren't simply stat based, but are new mechanics unique to them.
+ There are several secret areas (and routes to the throne) to discover. But a lot of these require the player to do obscure things that they would otherwise never do.
Disliked:

You'll need to be extra attentive to discover the difference certain mutations make. The amazingly detailed wiki and even game guide on Google Play Store makes this almost a moot point.

Miami has a new mass murderer, he might be doing good or he might be doing evil. But the only way you can find out is if you play this game.
So in this top down shooter you step into the blood spattered boots of two “hero’s” as they carve a bloody streak through Miami’s underworld. Now to say that this game is gory is an understatement, but due to its amazing retro art style the copious amounts of blood, guts and death seem little more than a fever dream, as does this game as a whole. The aesthetic is one that I found very like a comic book, I know it’s done in 16 bit but it’s so stylised, bright and vibrant that I was enthralled immediately.
The way the story draws you in is the same way a mad man scrawls his name in blood on the walls of his padded cell, that is to say both are fruit loops crazy but in my analogy at least the crazy guy is using his own blood and not hundreds of other peoples whom have the audacity to want to keep it all inside themselves and not share.
Now back to the story, you start off knowing nothing, you go on knowing a little more of nothing, until the game ends and you know a tiny bit more than if you hadn’t bothered starting. There’s a shadowy organisation using you to further their bloody campaign on crime but that’s about it. This is not to say the game isn’t compelling I found myself face stomping my way through goons at a rate Usain Bolt would be proud of just to see what would happen next and the endings, yes plural, two “hero’s” two endings do wrap the everything up quite well.
Now the game itself is for a lack of a better word, bloody fantastic. You can approach each stage in a huge number of different ways using a very large arsenal masks, one of your characters loves those and each one gives you different weapons or abilities. And whilst you may be content to just kill everything in sight and march all the way to the finale this game is actually a pretty well done score attack adventure and you would have missed most of the pleasure… and misery.
To get the best scores you have to complete every stage faster than lightning with as many different executions and combo kills under your belt as you can manage. This is where the challenge lies, the game itself is hard but to do it perfectly is insanely difficult but so rewarding that it’s crazy and you would be nuts to try. But since we are all psycho’s who love masochism have at it.
The sound track is great, but as is the standard for all games sent in the 80’s, I think it’s a law or something. The gameplay is phenomenal, you will fail a lot but every single time it is your fault, the game is punishing but not a cheater. I cannot recommend this enough for people who love a challenge. I had hours of fun and frustration in equal measure.

This is literally the game I have been waiting for since 4x4 EVO 2!
This is everything that i had hoped 'Off-Road Drive' would be (which i found to be a bitter disappointment)... The problem with that game is that it was way to focussed on racing, scoring points and cometition and not on the terrain or proper offroading 'feel'. Each section felt deliberate and distinct with absolute consistancy and there was no free roaming to be done, you always followed a track layed out for you. Spintires doesn't feel like this.
The areas feel natural and organic and every surface reacts in a certain way.  While there are paths in the jungle, you are not obliged to use them. There is no set route, competitors or time limits. It is simply you vs the enviroment.
Although a lot of people are saying it is too hard, i think the balance is really good; at the end of the day you dont get the fun of rescuing your trucks if they never get stuck. The difficulty also causes you to think about your actions and use inginuity to get from A to B. For instance, after loading my truck with logs I realised it was too heavy to make it back through deep mud. So I used the winch to connect another truck and used to power of both trucks to get through. This careful and conciderate style of playing is reinforced by the lack of competition; beacuse speed in unimportant you can take time to plan and think your way through differant obsticales.
The graphics are very good, and really show off the (superb) terrain deformation while the trucks themselves are very nicely rendered. But for me it is the physics that are the real pleaser. The virtual mud and water reacts in a really realistic way and the more times you use a specific path, the more emphasised those effects will be as the path detirorates. The vehicle's suspensions react in very differant ways depending on weight and sufaces, while the diff lock and AWD functions feel predictable and reliable. You really get a sense of feel and detail when you play this game.
The camera (that many are complaining about) can be very useful 70% of the time but really the game would benifit with more camera options as the remaining 30% of the time it is really useless; especially when using the crane or towing trucks, but with future improvements planned, plus a cockpit cam these problems should be temporary. The game's content is also fairly limited and doesnt consist of much more than exploring, picking up logs, dropping them off and rescuing the many  trucks you will roll over, total or get stuck. But again, more content is planned in future updates.
All things concidered this is a fantastic game, if you are a fan of any truck sims, driving games or just want a proper off-road game that is focussed on the challenge of the terrain and not time limits or competition then I would seriously reccommend this!

So, dear reader, this is as much a note to me as it is to you: don't play this any more - it's just frustrating.

First, a tl;dr version of my review...
+Everything that made Shadow of Mordor awesome, but with even MORE awesome stuff!
+Orc followers actually have personality now!
+Runs better on my PC
+Difficulty levels!  When the game's harder, you can better experience the nemesis system.
-Act 1 of the game is a bit tedious, especially if you don't care about the story and just want to kill orcs and build your army.
-While the plot is good, the execution in many cases needs serious work.
-WHY IS 'NO CHANCE' STILL A THING!?
-Loot boxes are cancer.
Now for a more extensive review
Like I said, it has everything that made Shadow of Mordor great, and many of them have even been improved!  The combat system is the same, but at least to me, feels more polished, though that may be a result of Shadow of War running better on my machine than its predecessor.
The game itself is by nature harder than its predecessor, even on 'normal' mode (Yes, I'm one of those plebs who played on normal.  I'm going to play through on Nemesis eventually).  In Shadow of War, by the time I got to the late game, NOTHING was a threat to me anymore.  The only time I would die would to be a random fluke, when I make a dumb mistake and get downed and am unlucky enough to be near a captain with the 'no chance' trait that SHOULDN'T EXIST.  I mean, seriously.  If it significantly reduced the time I had to succeed on my last chance, that's one thing, that's additional challenge, but to not get a chance at all?  I've died several times to captains with 'no chance' when they just got one hit in while my health was low.  It's BS.
Orc followers have personality!  What's more, you can assign them as bodyguards, so they can
follow you!  It's great!  Since your followers are no longer mindless zombies who carry out your orders, they now can betray you!  Sometimes the random betrayals are annoying, but they also keep the game interesting and allow some good stories to come out of them.  Same with the 'Blood Brother' trait.  It's easy to accidentally kill the blood brother of one of your followers, and they will betray you if you do, and I've had some good stories come about as a result, be it my quest to re-recruit them, to kill them, or make them
I had killed them.  An annoying glitch, though, is that sometimes when you shame a captain, they'll taunt you as if you had run away the next time they meet you... which doesn't make sense.
Loot and gear is improved, though it seems a tad bit tacked-on.  Most equipment you'll find isn't going to be particularly useful for anything other than destroying for Mirian.  While it is, I think, an improvement on the rune system from SoM, I think they tried to take it a step too far, because managing my inventory is more often than not a chore.  I'm not excited for any new loot I find, I just want to get it out of my inventory.  I'm not exactly sure where the balance would be here, but here they missed it.
Honestly this is the part of the review that I'm looking forward to writing the most... I'm not going to complain about it has no shame in curb-stomping, shredding, incinerating, and then dancing upon the grave of established Lord of the Rings Lore (though obviously I will mention it because I just did), because I think a certain amount of artistic license is allowed.  I'm not going to demand that they treat the books like a bible, but there are a few points where I think they strayed a bit further than makes sense; chief among them being turning Shelob, that big brutish spider, into a sexy sorceress in an evening gown.  I get that that they were running with some alternate continuity or something or other, but still... they could just have easily come up with a new and original character to be the sexy sorceress in an evening gown.  Heh, I guess I
complain about the divergence from the lore... but that's all the complaining I'm going to do.
Like I said, the overall plot is good.  I don't want to have to beat around the bush and take twice as long to say what I want to say, so
Honestly, while the plot itself is good and has twists that I didn't see coming, the writers did next to nothing to make me actually
about what happened to any of the characters, I never got any insight on what made many of the characters 'tick'.  And the dialogue... good crap, some of that dialogue...  Now, I don't think particularly highly of myself as a writer, but I know for a
that I could do better on developing the characters and with their dialogue than was done here.  A good example comes from early in the game, when Talion is talking to whatshisface, the general/king/whatever-he-is of Minas Ithil.  Honestly this guy was so forgettable that I don't remember his name or what his actual role was beyond being Idril's father/a traitor.  To summarize the dialogue, it goes like this.  This isn't exact wording, but I'm not even oversimplifying it.
That Guy: "A ranger from the Black Gate?  Good, we could use all the help we can get."
Talion:  "I'm not here to help, I'm here for the Palantir."
That Guy:  "Then protect the city.  But... we could use someone to kill their captains."
Talion:  "Okay."
I mean... what?  Normally the word 'but' precedes some kind of reversal, such as if he were going to say "but... help us repel these attackers and I'll take you to it," but that's not what he said!  I know that Talion wants to defend the city, and it's just Celibrimbor who wants only the Palantir, but still... show me some more deliberation!  What really makes this one exchange unforgivable; however, is the fact that it's
to improve.  Consider now, how I would write this exchange.
That Guy: "A ranger from the Black Gate?  Good, we could use all the help we can get."
Talion:  "I'm not here to help, I'm here for the Palantir."
That Guy:  "Then help us protect the city.  Target their captains and sow terror in their ranks, and once the attackers are gone I'll take you to it."
Talion:  "I'll hold you to that."
This isn't perfect, but it's still far, far better than what's actually in the game.  The real dialogue feels forced, that they just wanted to give an excuse for the players to go and kill a bunch of orcs (which is what the game's about), but they could have made it actually flow with just a bit of work to make it seem like the captain/traitor/forgettable-idiot was actually convincing Talion on what the best course of action was rather than just having Talion say "Okay!" and do what he's told like a child.
I'd go on a rant about other horribly handled plot points, and I intended to, but... I hit the character limit.  So I guess I'll have to skip forward to the conclusion.

Alan Wake is a strange game. Its story is somewhat good, but with really really bad dialogues. You simply don't want to hear them and don't give a flying **** for what people are saying in this game. Most of the time it's all irrelevant for the plot and aren't even funny or entertaining dialogues. You really, REALLY won't care at all, believe me.
Aside of this, Alan Wake has one of the most terrible level designs I ever experienced in my life. Most of the time you're on big open useless woods. They look like non linear, but you just follow the roads or some easy visual language signs and you're right on your way. Instead of what it looks like, it is totally linear. All the rest of the scenery are just useless(except from one place or another where you can find some collectables or weapon caches. But they're not even that hard to find...). Not only that but, also, most of the time you will be walking in these useless woods without ANYTHING happening at all. A literal "walking simulator", for the most part.
Besides, Alan Wake have a "ok" gameplay with interesting mechanics. But it's a shame that you'll only see this game shining(ba dum tss) in very few moments. There's one part or another in this game where you'll think something like "THAT'S what I was expecting from this game!". It's really a shame that most of the time you will not be thinking this, but will be like "oh my god, how could be this is a game? I absolutely love fallout 1 and 2, and when I first watched the Kickstarter trailer for this game I was seriously foaming at the mouth. Another top-down isometric, post-apocolyptic RPG made by some of the same people that gave birth to the Fallout series? I was so hopeful...

Instead of using a locked perspective like in the original Fallout games, they opted for a 360 degree fully-rotatable camera. What could be wrong with that? EVERYTHING. If you walk around a corner you dissapear, and you cannot click on or move your characters without first rotating the camera untill you can (sort of) see where you are going. This gets unbelievably frustrating, especially when indoors or near tall objects (which is basically all the time) and there is nothing you can do about it. Period. It is just a poor design.
I might even have been able to look past the terrible camera if there were some nice graphics to look at. Sadly there are none to be found. Textures and models are simple and flat, the UI is ugly, feels cheap, and didn't scale properly to my screen resolution.

Lots of reviews of this game says "This game isn't as bad as the metacritic score says it is" or "This game has improved a lot since the original." Sorry to say, but if this game improved a lot, it wasn't much of a game to begin with. There's no tutorial at all so you're forced to jump into one of th five or so game modes all of which pales in comparison to survival. There's versus and capture the flag, but it's no Left 4 Dead--that is, the balance is totally off. All the dinosaurs suck except for the T-rex who can toss instadowning rocks (OP) and who can instakill any person close enough to them by swallowing them whole (Super OP). There's other dinosaurs who all boil down to Dinosaurs who all suck and the T-rex. There's tiny dinos who die in like 3 seconds of getting shot or the big ones who can survive getting shot, but who have problems getting kited all day. The marines don't have much variation in viable choices either. There's the assault, the support, the scout, and the assassin--all of whom gets their asses ran over by the hordes of dinosaurs except for the assault who has a jetpack that lets him sits in the mountains on the edge of the map and allows him to pick off the dinosaurs one-by-one while being untouchable to them.
Sure this game (or any game) is a steal at $1 but after about 2 hours of playing I had enough as I got bored of sitting up in a mountain peak and shooting down at the dinosaurs, running around to random checkpoints for unexplained goals throughout  the map for up to at least 5 minutes, and playing games where people were only OP T-rexes or OP Assaults. The most fun I had in this game was driving around in a car and running over dinos while I was spamming #Orion:Driving Hit & Run Simulator but that and the game gets old very fast as you soon realize every map is just an excuse to get to random waypoints for no reason which just slow down gameplay just to shoot more dinosaurs.

I backed this one on Kickstarter, mainly because there was a goal set to fund a
Linux version and there was only a few games for Linux then. The idea sounded
good – reviving an old classic, something like Fallout, multiple skills and
ways to solve quests, etc.
After over two years of waiting it came. Playing it was tricky at first, due to
a 'fog of war bug' on my integrated Intel GPU. It seems the problem was known
from early beta but all the developers could say was 'Intel GPUs are not
supported'. Oh… and I thought the game was supposed to be about story,
playability and reviving classic. Nothing that should require a dedicated
gaming hardware. Current laptop should be enough. And is enough when the
workaround for the bug is known. But creators would not acknowledge that – buy
a gaming computer or don't bother us.
OK, so with the workaround for the GPU bug the game was fun to play. There were
some game bugs, sometime ruining some quests, but nothing making the game
unplayable. I have played 60 hours… and got bored. 'Dozens of skills' really
means 'many different ways to open containers' all the same containers all the
time. It is a game of opening chests and safes. And digging holes.
Yes, there is also the combat and combat skills. You need good hand gun or
sniper skills not to kill your own people by mistake… But there are also high
explosives, which you need not skill to use at all. Always 100% hit chance,
always 100% deterministic effects. How can it be? If not the price and
availability explosives would be the most effecting and safest method of fight.
Then come the patches. Some bugs were fixed, often for parts I have already
played and do not wish to come back. Some features were implemented. And you
know what? Linux is not an equal platform now. Steam achievements were
introduced two patches ago and they are 'Windows only'. Steam achievements!
I could understand, that some advanced graphics or sound effects could be
tricky to do in Linux, or that handling some exotic controller could be
impossible. But the achievements?!
It is not that Wasteland 2 is a bad game or that my contribution was waste of
money, but I am a bit disappointed and the game is not worth the 'user reviews'
rating it has now.
BTW I got bored by Fallout 2 too, so if you really love this type of games you could probably ignore my opinion.

Umm, haven't played much yet, but so far first impressions are good!
It is the modern day version of what Fallout 3 should have been.
It is also what the next Jagged Alliance # should have been I guess (only played 1 and 2).
It has everything you would expect from an improved version of the ones above, except for a tutorial on some gameplay and interaction elements that would be good to know, before you spend 10 minutes clicking around in vain. Otherwise clean interface with some nice "extra" functionanility. For example: other party members' abilites colored and listed while hovering over current characters abilities and such quality of life improments. Small details like this meam a lot while playing, because you don't have to spend time looking through them trying to memorize it all.
The gameplay is fun so far, controls need getting used to (right click vs left click situations are a mess). Combat feels alright, although I'm haveing a hard time to see if I can hide behind some objects or not. I'll get used to it I guess.
Talking is also great, feels fresh to me after all the shorthand quest descriptions and meaningless and lifeless banter of recent games (thinking of WoW/Skyrim/Fallout:NV...)
Graphics are vivid and have a nice style, although performance is questionable sometimes. It doesn't really matter as this is not a snap-shot kind of game.
Sounds are allright so far, I just hope not all guns of the same type will sound the same. Voice acting is surprisingly good compared to the almost cheesy and ridiculous amature cam intro! That was a shocker, mostly because I didn't expect it! Maybe it was done to set your standards lower, before actually starting the game :D j/k
Anyways, If you enjoyed the gameplay Fallout 1 2, Jagged Alliance, or any games similar to those, AND you like post-nuclear end-of-the-world stories, Buy it!
one little personal note: it requires long play-sessions to enjoy. Don't expect to sit down for 10 mins and get something deep and worthy done in that time. Don't even try to do that, it just ruins the experience! Enjoy it like you would enjoy a properly good book, take your time, read every line. It's so much more worth it than running through it!

Mafia 3 is a complicated game to say the least. It's also been a fair bit controversial based on it's PC release and its content matter. But if you can look behind the controversy, you will find a gem in story telling that raises the bar in my opinion. The cutscenes are entertaining to watch, as well as the voice acting being top notch. The cutscenes kinda feel like you are watching a great movie. The gameplay is also well handled, and I haven't had any problems with the gameplay.
However, there are a few problems that people need to be aware of, but they shouldn't be absolute dealbreakers. First, the game does have a tendency to crash, even if you are running the latest graphics drivers. Second, the graphic fidelity seems like it was downgraded to fit consoles, and since it's a port, they didnt get this upgraded in time. Finally, there are a fair bit of glitches but I've only seen these 2nd hand, game's ran fine for me in that respect. I assume that Hangar 13 is working on this though as they were quick on their fps fix, taking only a day to implement it.
There are still haters that say this game sucks because it isnt like the past Mafia games, but nonetheless, if you want a good action game with a great narrative and storyline, look no further than Mafia 3.
TL;DR
Pros:
- Story is top notch, and I've only played 5 hours so far.
- Gameplay is handled well, with multiple approaches to an encounter possible.
- Music is amazing, they really handled this part of the game well.
- Cutscenes and Voice Acting are also really well done, and are some of the best I've seen.
- Developers fixed an issue within 1 day of game being released and willing to listen to feedback.
Cons:
- Graphics aren't as good as they could be, seems like a console port issue that can be fixed though.
- Game tends to crash a few times, although this seems like another engine issue that can be fixed with time.
- Some glitches that can break the game (I haven't encountered these... yet)
- The PC fanbase... zing!
Final Verdict: 8.5/10
Suggestion: Buy Now or Wait for Sale.

Natural Selection 2 is everything that makes a shooter great. Never before have I seen an asymmetric shooter that has so much love to detail and balance. It has good variety in weapons and "enemies" while making sure there is no such thing as useless equipment. Everything has a use and is viable, be it the starting rifle, the side pistol or the first alien life form.
This game promotes and, indeed, needs team play and communication. An absolute fantastic online experience best enjoyed in 7v7 or 8v8 matches so to not lose the tactical feel as well as the importance of every individual involved.
However, it is important to say that this game has an incredibly steep learning curve and will take several hours to even get your head around. Especially the role of the commander should not be taken before completely understandly the flow and priorities of matches as well as tactics. I myself have not filled the com station until 40 hours into the game for it is the most stressful and important position in every match. The community is very much aware of this learn curve and is, in general, very eager to explain the many questions beginners might have. And don't shy away from learning the alien side! It is an asymmetric shooter, after all.
I can not recommend this game more appart from the dwindling player base as this game continues to age. It is definately my favorite shooter of all times and I really hope this game will see a continuation even though I would be just as happy with just a revival of the once large player base. Giving it a 10 would not suffice. This game has heavily influenced what I expect of online shooters to come.

I had pretty high hopes for Crashlands, being a game that advertises a ton of my interests. I've had it on my wishlist for a while and was really happy to see it on sale in the running Humble Bundle sale, but after just a few hours, I feel that Crashlands has already overstayed its welcome with me.
The combat system is as simple as you'd expect from a 2D top-down game, but it's pieced together very well. Each type of enemy has a different attack pattern as well as a special attack that is used at random. I also wouldn't expect for a game like this to offer quests, but I'm glad that they're available and I hope that similar games do this in the future.
After an hour or two of playing, you've already done everything that Crashlands has to offer. Collect resources A, B, and C to craft workbench 1. Collect resources D, E, and F to craft workbench 2. This is Crashlands. While I'm a fan of grindy games, the grind is only fun if the end result feels rewarding, but, in the case of Crashlands, it isn't. Each workstation will offer more or less the same craftable items as the last, just with slightly higher stats. After 6 hours of playing, I'm currently using tier 9 gear and I'm not interested enough to keep grinding.
The game moves a bit too slowly. As a game that focuses heavily on exploration, most of your time spent in Crashlands is exploring new areas. Your character walks slowly and you'll quickly realize that, aside from slighly different enemies and resorces, areas don't feel or look much different. I never felt that I was actually going on an adventure in my exploration and I never found new things that I thought were interesting. I wanted to find secrets, dangers, and rewards that other exploration games offer, but Crashlands doesn't have them. These levels of repetition make Crashlands terribly boring.
Maybe my expectations have set me up for disappointment, but the store page is a bit misleading with some of the terms used. Calling the game an ARPG and claiming over 500 craftable items doesn't match up with what the game offers. Yes, there's technically over 500 craftable items, but think of RuneScape's bronze, iron, and steel items. If a sequel of Crashlands were to be made that had a better focus on these aspects, I feel that it would do very well and I'd be a big fan of it.

I first played this game when my (at the time) 11 year old nephew showed it to me on his iPhone. I immediately noticed something, it was very similar to Don't Starve. The two games are so similar, in fact, that if you  swapped skin and music between the two games, not much would change.
With that said, this game is also very different from Don't Starve. Where DS you are constantly worrying about the threat of starvation, freezing to death, or being attacked by any sort of horrible monster, Crashlands is different. Crashlands takes place in a sci-fi fantasy world. It also has an obvious storyline as well as easy to follow quests.
It is also a much more light hearted game than Don't Starve. It's utterly without doom and gloom. To say one is better than the other isn't fair, because again, while they are extremely similar, they are also unique. What I would say is if you liked Don't Starve, you will definitely like this. If you've never played Don't Starve, I still think you would enjoy this game. It's very good, has lots of replayability and tons of stuff to do and build and craft.

I was looking for a shoot 'em up style game to play so I happened to stumble upon Beekyr Reloaded. After watching the videos to decide if I should purchase the game, my interest piqued. The gameplay and premise reminded me of Insector-X and Kolibri so I hit that purchase button right away. After installation, I booted up the game and began playing. Seconds into the first game and the game pauses on me and I get the following message; "Beekyr is running slow" or something to that effect. OK, so I go to the options screen, go to graphic settings and turn off high detail, particle effects, etc. Restart the game again, and I get a little further into the first stage and when I least expect it, I get the game running slow message again. All graphic setting are set to the lowest settings so this time I close any extra windows and programs running in the background and restart the game again. Guess what? "Game running slow" message pops up. By this time, I'm frustrated and I request a refund. There's absolutely no way to enjoy the game if "Game running slow" messages keep popping up and interupting gameplay. Thanks, but no thanks.

That's just a list I've come up with on the spot, I'm sure I missed some pros and cons, but you can get an idea of how the game is hopefully.

absolutely addicted! I would like to some day work on my "real" pilots license. However, money and time don't allow that right now. Microsoft Flight Simulator X teaches real life aviation skills, and has a training course with one of aviation's finest instructors, Rod Machado. While this course won't count as ground school or F.A.A. training, it will give you close to real life training and flight instruction. Technical stuff - I downloaded the game directly from the Steam website for 50% off. This was a lot cheaper and better than ordering from Amazon and waiting for the download code. While downloading did take over night, once the game was up and running it was pretty real life with only minor glitches. The download process is cumbersome though, try to give it at least several hours to download with plenty of "stops" (pop ups) on the way. My computer is a very low end budget model (Intel Celeron 2.16 GHz, 4.00 GB RAM, 64 bit OS, x64 based processor) and the game runs fine with little lag. I am very pleased with this program, and look forward to more great software from Steam!

Alan Wake is a strange game. Its story is somewhat good, but with really really bad dialogues. You simply don't want to hear them and don't give a flying **** for what people are saying in this game. Most of the time it's all irrelevant for the plot and aren't even funny or entertaining dialogues. You really, REALLY won't care at all, believe me.
Aside of this, Alan Wake has one of the most terrible level designs I ever experienced in my life. Most of the time you're on big open useless woods. They look like non linear, but you just follow the roads or some easy visual language signs and you're right on your way. Instead of what it looks like, it is totally linear. All the rest of the scenery are just useless(except from one place or another where you can find some collectables or weapon caches. But they're not even that hard to find...). Not only that but, also, most of the time you will be walking in these useless woods without ANYTHING happening at all. A literal "walking simulator", for the most part.
Besides, Alan Wake have a "ok" gameplay with interesting mechanics. But it's a shame that you'll only see this game shining(ba dum tss) in very few moments. There's one part or another in this game where you'll think something like "THAT'S what I was expecting from this game!". It's really a shame that most of the time you will not be thinking this, but will be like "oh my god, how could be this is a game? I'm only walking and walking" or "What a REALLY bad level design!" or "This game is SO frustrating! How can they throw me 10 enemies when I'm totally unarmed??" and things like these...
I'm really disappointed with this game. Shame. These guys from remedy gave us the perfectly crafted Max Payne and now it's really hard to believe that they gave us a game like Alan Wake...

I wish I could give this a neutral rating. But having to choose positive or negative, I'd say positive in the end except for some complaints / bad design decisions:
1. Monotonous grind in Act 4. You're going to be doing the same thing over and over again defending your fortress, or if you fail, attacking numerous times in order to get the best ending.
2. RNG. You might come up on a warlord that has the worst immunities/strengths possible and you're going to have to kill him somehow in order to capture a fortress and progress. Maybe you should visit the in-game store and get some loot chests? *bleh*
3. Betrayal system. This shouldn't even be there in my opinion. If you recruit someone they should stay in their ranks, it doesn't add any value to gameplay, only to lengthen the game time.
4. Sticky controls. What I mean when traversing rooftops or other objects, the character sticks to ledges too easily. Sometimes the simplest tasks such as jumping off or trying to climb down are a pain.
5. No Chance. Sometimes you might get stunlocked by an enemy and a captain with No Chance finishes you off. It happens and its /facepalm time. Also, the extra talent to give you second chance at come back gets negated by it.
6. Balancing issues, this is both be a curse and a blessing. As you keep defending you fortress in Act 4, the enemies obviously get stronger. There's a tactic that I have been employing to get through Act 4 easily, yes it cheapens the gameplay, by then again, when you're doing the same thing over and over again without any reward, mind as well do it.I don't want to spoil it but it simply makes the gameplay stale. I`ll just say that some skills are overpowered such as the "blink" dominate.
7. No dialogue skip. This one is by far one of the most enraging aspects of the game. You cannot skip a dialogue from a captain/commander/warlord. Its kinda sad to see some low level captain ambush and taunt you for 30 seconds just to be slaughtered in the next moment. In the sieges later on, you will be sitting and waiting for the dialogue to finish for over a minute when the enemy gets into your fortress and 3-4 captains show up at once (multiply that by the number of waves incoming). This simply bad game design in my opinion. Also, you'll hear the same taunts over and over again as you progress through the game...
8. "War Chests" I could care less about someone else wanting to spend money for in-game items. Yes, in my opinion its dumb, but then again, it's their money. The reason I categorize it as a con is that many games are implementing this and along with DLC it just shortens/ruins gameplay in the end.
With DLC, you usually have content cuts. And with loot boxes, using Shadow of War as an example, you have game design decisions that center around them (RNG strengths/weaknesses, monotonous grind, overlords level up if you fail to overtake the fortress). The mindset around designing games lately has been in the wrong direction with some major releases (Cow Doody WII, Shadow of War, Assassin's Creed: Origins, Deus Ex: Mankind Divided) to name a few. Hopefully this might change in the future.
I'd say go ahead get this if you like spending 30+ hours in a game and if you liked the first one. Otherwise be preppared to rage if you're not used to the series.

M-E: Shadow of War... That indeed is a title to any nerd and/or geek that has read Tolkiens books, so instantly you have high hopes and expectations for the title.. In my case its more or less "
."
I'll try to keep this review short but with a valid and simple core to help you understand why
haven't enjoyed this game too much.
For me games should be an adventure, you know, depth, pace, experience, twists, surprises and this game for the most  part was. Really good story, first 20-30 hours were well paced with side guests and collectables, this game had 110% of my attention in every bit of the story and collectibles, every single alphabeth in every word. It was amazing to try and find each and every bit of the story to understand more of this world... But thats mostly all the game really offered me personally.
As a gamer that has played, reviewed and experienced hundreds games and tens to hundreds of thousands of hours of different gameplay, the skilltrees were a mess. Anyone who knows how to screw around, have fun but still be efficient orc slaying machine would know that 70-80% of the skills and "upgrades" were below "optional". Why go with an ability that increases your might from Stealth kills, that hardly really matters when you have to fight 90% of the game 1.vs.legion, than with an ability that triples your Might generation from successful attacks, that works well with chain executions that you can almost every 4th or 5th attack (2-3 crits, which also comboes well with crit abilities) chain to kill and stack your hit-streak on multiple orcs, instakilling them and giving you an instant edge in the battle? Or you can use that might to insta drain/dominate orcs, or deal different types of aoe dot effects and wiping that army down instantly. I dont understand, it hardly lets you be creative with your builds and playstyles.
Lets talk about gear, which is also a good part of the game... And it bored me. Early Legendaries are boring, leveling them up is like going to the gym... but already exhausted for banging your neighbors daughter. Legendaries a re supposed to be Legendary, tho you seem to find 1 legendary orc after 3 turns... Wheres the "legendary" in that?.. And when you finaly level them up to 60, they are so underwhelming and seen so far into the game... But I gotta say that the set bonuses lets you screw around with possible builds.
And not gonna waste too much on the Orcs. Yeah, some of them are unique...
(♥♥♥♥ing love my Tower orc thats Cursed, boosts other Savages,  is immune to all effects and has tremendous amount of health with a butt loads  of other perks, and is not even Legendary, but Epic <_> )
...But leveling them up, "gearing" them up well and correctly, fighting some of them... Its just too grindy even for me.. And I have spent around 10 years on WoW non-stop, which is around 20k hours. I like grinding a lot, some times it satisfying when done well (Warframes combat keeps the grind amazing. WoW's combat and the feeling of success when you finaly get that one Achievement, even tho it doesnt do jack...) I cant say that this game grindfest satisfying at all... Either sitting there for 3 minutes to Pokemon your orcs, or babysitting them on an ambush is just boring, not rewarding...
Combat is also a big meh. Its uncomplicatedly complicated. You press couple of buttons, thats it. Then you face against an orc  that can only be killed with stealth attacks, and there you go running  around the fortress for 40 minutes stealthing him and hoping the ♥♥♥♥er doesn't adapt in time... Or use his weakness and daze him to lay hell upon him... But good luck finding a ♥♥♥♥ing graug in the middle of a fortress...
Its not a bad game, but nowhere close of being a masterpiece. Its just Good, Average, Meh, Good waste of couple of hours waiting for your friends to come Online.
P.S: If theres any grammar errors, or something I should've put differently to have it make more sense, notify me, please.

Shadow of War has improved on almost everything from Shadow of Mordor (besides a few bugs) and then ruined it all with their loot boxes.
As you probably know, loot boxes give you weapons, orcs, orc powerups and XP boosts.
You can buy the low level loot boxes with the in game Silver you get, and you get a lot of it. You can also pony up and spend real money on Gold to buy high level loot boxes (you can also get some Gold from daily challenges).
And the result of the loot boxes is that
.
In Shadow of Mordor, the only way to get loot was killing captains. Getting a powerful weapon was an achievement. You would send death threats to the most powerful captains, making them more powerful, learn their weaknesses, then have a really tough fight to beat them. Now I can spend some of my free in game silver money to get a loot box which gives me 2 fairly decent bits of loot. The sense of acheivement is gone completely, there is literally no incentive to kill captains now, its always better to recruit them.
Then there are the orcs. It seems like they have decided to make the game massive and grindy near the end to encourage you to fast track some of that by buying orcs loot boxes. So they made the end of the game super boring and repetitive because of the loot boxes.
The very fact that loot boxes are in a game means they will want to provide incentives to buy them, which results in creating time consuming elements to encourage people to skip them. Its the same as what happened to mobile games, but now we are seeing it in full priced AAA games and it is resulting in a game that is boring as hell in the second part.
I, like other reviewers, haven't finished the game, because it is not fun to play after a certain point.
I loved Shadow of Mordor and prepurchased Shadow of War, and yes I thoroughly enjoyed the short time I have played, but I am sad that loot boxes turned this game from a gem into a turd. I honestly looked forward to this since the first game and I am bitterly disappointed.

In this case, the difficulty is riged to screw you over.  Case in point.  I have a 0% jam factor on one of my guns which should mean it never jams.  Am I right???  On easy, it would never jam. How about critical hits you may say.  60% on a blade you may say = 1/10 chance to crit.  While their team of whom is infinite, may have a 5% chance to crit but crits every hit and unless you have cover they never miss.
So to sum this game up.  If you like a story and are willing to never leave easy mode behind.  These people should be the only group happy about this game.  So go play it.  Otherwise, don't waste your money on this shallow boring game until they release mod tools to fix this broken system.

If, like me, you played the original, especially on first release, you HAVE to play Wasteland 2.  There will be some VERY familiar characters, places, scenarios, and missions.  This updated version takes place several years after the first, perhaps a decade or more, but stays very true to the original Wasteland, something other post-apocalypse games (I'm looking at you Fallout series) have tried and never quite accomplished.  Even the mechanics and UI, while completely modern, feel very familiar.  The story is top-notch, and the world, as true to the original, feels the weight of the player's footsteps and those footprints persist.  Early on, your characters will all feel the same, but you do have to invest in diversified specializations, giving each character a unique feel.  The engine has been vastly improved since original early access and runs super smoothly.  Other interface problems, issues and complaints have been rectified, and patches and post-release maintenance have been timely.  Solid, thoroughly enjoyable game from a solid, committed developer.  What more can you ask for?  Well, for me, the only thing I find missing (spoiled by Skyrim, I guess) is the ability to switch into first person more.  Had this been designed in, Wasteland 2 would be very near to perfection for me.  And that's my only complaint, really, the camera.  Sometimes you want to get in a bit closer, to see what your character is seeing, to set up line of sight down a scope, to see your bludgeoning up close and personal, what have you.  Maybe in Wasteland 3?  Hopefully it doesn't take another quarter century for that to happen.

Post Patch Review:
Really fun, narrative driven open world. Have to knock it for being alittle unrealistic(all the shooting and killing in the entire game combined  is only about 50% of what actually happens in New Orleans). Story can best be summed up as an "if Django Unchained and Goodfellas had a baby" type affair. So far the narrative pacing is quite good, with a great first couple of hours really selling the setting and getting you accustomed to how the rest of the story structure is built. Gameplay is solid though alittle janky at times for a modern third person game, but complaints in this area are minor. If you've played previous Mafia games then you already have a base understanding of how getting around the world feels. Atmosphere is great and the soundtrack is a highlight. Driving around the faux NOLA, outrunning cops while "Sympathy for the Devil" blares is always a thrill. Graphics, at max settings, are at times gorgeous, and others underwhelming. Since the patch, I've been able to run the game smoothly locked at 60 and this has enhanced the look but overall details in the world seem lacking when placed against others in this genre. Though to clarify its not an ugly game by any means. Motion capture really a stand out in this category. In summation, I think it's a really solid game with a loving crafted story that keeps you interested from one story hook to the next. If you liked previous games in the series or mob movies then you'll find plenty to love here.

ORION: Dino Horde is a wonderful game involving, yes, you guessed it, pigs. The game opens up new possibilities in the genre of first-pigson shooters. It includes a variety of maps and gamemodes to spice up the normal pig-shooter formula, and many customizations to make your pig stand out from the rest. Additionally, the visuals in the game truly shine. I was amazed at the Xbox One's new pig physics engine, where even the curly tail is visible and incredibly detailed. Compared to the predecessor, ORION: Dino Beatdown, pig AI is vastly improved. Instead of running around attacking you for no reason, the enemies now act like real pigs! You can play as many different classes of humans to take down the evil pigs, such as Medic, Medic, and Medic. The Medic class is my personal favorite. As for the modes, there is classic Survival, Conquest (a longer version of survival), Gun Game, Team Deathmatch, and more. It even contains a rampage mode where you can play as a pig! I had a lot of fun oinking my way to victory against 3+ friends.
Overall, ORION: Dino Horde is a masterpiece. Spiral Game Studios has made a huge leap in game design. The game benefits greatly from new capabilities of next-gen gaming, and provides a new and refreshing experience for those tired of pig-related FPS. I give the game a solid 4/5 stars.

Wasteland 2 hearkens back to the day when a 7% chance to fail meant failing 3 out of 4 times, and a game would beat your♥♥♥♥♥into the ground for the first hour or two, and then dramatically ease up after you get to sink a few skill points into your characters.
I'm not sure whether it's more appropriate to say that this game is Wasteland 2 or Fallout 3D, given it owes so much to the original Fallout, which in turn owes a lot to the original Wasteland. In any case, if you've played any of the original isometric Fallout games, then you will be right at home playing Wasteland 2 as the locations, world map, sound track, random encounters, combat, sense of humour, and missions all hold strong comparisons. Also, interestingly, there are positive aspects of the combat that are borrowed from XCOM: Enemy Unknown as well.
But that's not to say that this is just knock off - Wasteland 2 is deeply linked to the original Wasteland in its lore and the developers have learnt from the long gap between releases and taken the best of the old and the new and combined them to create a well-designed and deeply entertaining product.
Speaking of well-designed, as much as I generally dislike what Early Access has done to Steam, this is one of the games that has clearly benefitted from the system as you can spot numerous little features that have been implimented to improve the game's basic playability and fun-factor. Things like a button to sell all your junk at once, comparisons between the weapon you want to buy and the weapon you have, a solid log book that displays your missions, a button that reveals all objects that you can interact with, and the choice to automatically distribute your loot intelligently to the people who would use it best. All these things and more save the player time, eliminate clunky inventory management or frustrating moments when you don't know where to go or what to click - issues that were all too common in the heyday of isometric games.
Wasteland 2 is a loving heir to the original, and exists as a well-designed gem in a genre that typically suffers from over-complexity, suffering little of the clunkiness that one might expect from what one could call a 'throwback'. Its world is real and believable, the combat is fun (even if, at times, the hit chance feels skewed) and its characters are numerous, colourful and well-acted.
I highly recommend this to anyone who loved the original Wasteland, any of the Fallout games, or indeed anyone who likes a well-optimised RPG.

Review for Act 1
While playing video games growing up I've come to realize that the best games always seem to have something very specific in common; something that allows you get wrapped up in and immersed in a different world to escape reality for a short time and get lost in the beauty of it; and that would be that they all have a great story. A story first above all else; above crazy graphics, above gameplay, and even above music, etc.  A story that lets you become a part of it.
There are so many games these days that seem to forget that you should always start with that good story first, with fully realized worlds and the characters that inhabit them. And the games that do realize what should come first, usually turn out to be amazing works of art; games that draw you in and never let go, and have a lasting impression.
And Broken Age is an excellent example of this. The story is at the heart of the experience and you can feel it.
And even though this game might seem very simplistic in nature (given its gameplay style), it truly is just as satisfying to play as it would be to play a huge, multi-million dollar, RPG production made by a first-party studio by hundreds of people. But I think that's what makes this game so special: that it can be as great as it is even though it was made by just a handful of dedicated people who truly care about what they’re creating and why they’re creating it.
Double Fine has shown that you can have an exciting adventure that whisks you away to worlds full of challenges, laughter, and even emotionally-engaging moments, in the form of a point-and-click adventure that’s very accessible and easy to pick up and play. And the impact you feel at the end of Act 1 is an immensive one, that really gets you thinking. It was surprising to find out how much I cared about what happened to the two main characters and how they impacted the worlds around them.
I would definitely recommend this game to people who enjoy a great story, even if the gameplay style isn’t normally what they might be in to. You just might be surprised with how much you’ll enjoy it.
I absolutely cannot wait until Act II! I cannot wait to go back into Shay's and Vella's worlds to finally get some answers to some burning questions! And I have a feeling it's going to be a very satisfying conclusion regardless of how it ends.
:)
Congrats again to Double Fine for some amazing work so far!

Hard to recommend this game... and also hard to not recommend it.
The mixed feelings are a must because of the -extreme- grinding nature of the game: the game mechanic is very simple, where you basically roam around farming resources to build a workbench, to farm some more to build tools and items with which you can farm better resources to build better workbenches... and so on.
There's a small twist regarding pets where you can basically grind for an egg from every enemy type, and raise it as sidekick and upgrade them with recipes.
There are many technical shortcomings which create an unnecessarily difficult game because of artificial difficulty, but the most important are two: inventory slots are 4, and you can't swap equipment during fights, and enemy levels change with your level so you get basically one shotted by every enemy in the same game scenario (there's 3 and you can / need  get back to past levels to farm necessary resources).
In conclusion:
purchase this if you don't care about mindless, time-consuming and repetitive menial tasks, that can actually feel therapeutic for some people. Also purchase this if you don't mind a permanent irritating experience of being one shotted by every enemy of your same level (they have basically 10 times your health, and you regularly deal one tenth of their damage).
On the bright side apparently, the repetition of it all is a relaxing experience for some, probably diluted by the considerable amount of quests available and the funny dialogue and characters.
P.S.: i would have straight NOT recommended this solely for the -utter- and -disgusting- difficulty of the very last game boss, but it'd have been too much, and I basically forced myself to finish the game after I realized I was beyond 50% completion to quit it without ending it :(

Broken Age - Act 1 is a nice and short point-and-click adventure with an interesting out-of-this-world story, beautiful artwork, professional voice-acting and lovable details.
+ Interesting story-lines
+ Very nice graphics
+ Very good voice-acting
+ Forwarding of dialogue and animation
+ Pauseable cut-scenes
+ Dialogue choice by number keys
+ Reasoning: NPC feeling hunted by trees boards up window
+ Star Trek reference
+ Extend-A-Ladder
- Rather short
- Inventory items need to be dragged in order to use them
- Reasoning: NPC in predicament, PC refuses to help
- Reasoning: Wants to get fruit, finds a way up the tree, simply jumps down again
- Reasoning: Boarded up fireplace with fire
- Achievements are not yet activated it seems
The game has some nice and some bad design decisions. I disliked the fact that you have to drag items from the inventory, I prefer clicking the item and then the target. I really liked forwarding of animation and text passages. For some reason initial configuration has you press spacebar for forwarding. I recommend changing that to the middle mouse button and I'd much rather have this as a secondary function for left-click or right-click since both don't serve any purpose in those cases where forwarding can be employed.
I also like that you can pause cut-scenes and that dialogue options can be chosen by pressing number keys.
Initially the game showed me a black screen when starting the game with the menu music playing. This was finally resolved by updating my Catalyst Control Center. By then I had already followed some other advice to turn off the Steam overlay for the game and I had to restart Steam to get that back into the game(s).
The game has already defined achievements but they are not yet activated. From the global stats you can see that no one has any achievements and that they cover some actions in Act 1 and mostly actions outside it.
The game includes some strange reasoning, one instance I found funny but the rest was irritating.
* There is the morbid notion of a lumberjack boarding up his place in order to keep out trees.
* The lumberjack also boarded up his fireplace which has a fire burning inside at the time.
* The player character shows some false sense of modesty when refusing to help a stranger in need of assistance because that would include touching.
* At some point you have to get fruit from a tree and find a way up the tree.. from where the PC simply jumps down again.
There are a number of nice details in the game. I particularly like the two Star Trek TNG references and the "Extend-A-Ladder". The latter reminded me of the Grim Fandango scythe and triggered a warm bout of nostalgia.
I'm looking forward to playing Act 2 of Broken Age and recommend the first one.

I just want the game to end... This second half of this game has been easily one of my least favorite gaming experiences ever. I've never wanted a game to just end because it's been bothering me so much.
The first half of this game was great, I truly enjoyed it. I was really getting into the story and I was coming across some orcs that I formed some bonds with. I was hearing complaints about the late game, but I'm always one to look at things on the lighter side and give things a chance.
Once you get to the Shadow Wars bit after Act 3 this game is an utter chore to play. At this point I've put over 30 hours in and all I want is to finish the damn game and never have to touch it again. All of those forts you've captured to this point get ready to defend them over and over and over and over and over. Sure the first time you assault a fort or defend a fort is cool. But they really pound that whole practice into submission in the second half of this game and they don't change it up in the slightest. The enemy orcs level up and you're forced to either grind out leveling your guys at an unbelievably slow rate, or buy some loot boxes for a game that shouldn't have anything like that in the first place. Sure you can obtain the boxes through playing the game w/o buying them with real money, but you've got to earn the funds in game through grinding some more. A large portion of my late game has been going to the fight pit, sending in my low level orc just to have him die to a high level one to recruit that one in it's place. I've done this for what seems a hundred times now.
I was a big fan of the first game and I was greatly anticipating the sequel here. Things looked to be going alright, but it's been completely squandered and I can't believe it's gotten this bad. Microtransactions have completely ruined this game and they truly have no business being in the game anyway. This is a practice that needs to die before it destroys another what should have been great game.

But overall, in my opinion, this game is above brilliant and just short of fantastic.

It's a good game, not a great horror though. It plays pretty much like a zombie version of uncharted (not so much like TLoU, which is actually a lot more scary), so don't expect to be frightened of just about anything in this game, there is no surprises that will make you jump out of your sofa (provided you play with a controller - it works perfectly)... I personally don't play horror games much since they just make me stressed out and I play singleplayer games mostly to chill, so it's actually a plus for me. Either way the story is pretty interesting however it does lack the insane ending plot twists of uncharted. I was waiting for some crazy revelation at the end but either it didn't happen or I didn't quite catch it.
What I liked was that even though the levels are linear there is a small degree of exploration in each one, you always know where to go but there are off the path areas which you are not really forced to explore and you might find some bonus equipment there. And I loved how you don't actually need to go loot every single enemy you kill to get ammo like in tomb raider, forcing you to go on looting runs from body to body, here all the ammo is neatly distributed along your path or found when you go explore surrounding interiors or caves. I liked the small details like the Night Springs TV show episodes that you can decide to watch when you encounter a TV set or radio talk show that you can tune in to listen, the game is all around very well polished. Game gives you a relaxing feeling during daytime when no possessed people are around and you feel like you're just taking a drive etc, however if the night time was a bit more scary this feeling would be enhanced I guess.
There is only a few things I didn't like - the zombie waves appearing out of thin air just about every 20 meters felt like a little bit of a grind. It's not so bad as it sounds but seriously, the concept of enemies just appearing all around you because you step on an invisible script trigger feels kinda stupid as opposed to the enemies just lurking around the woods in front of you (and the game could definitely benefit from some kind of stealth/sneaking mechanism!).
Also your guy (Alan Wake) could use a bit more stamina, it's a bit frustrating when your character is out of breath and refuses to run while getting chased by an army of enemies waving machetes and chainsaws. That doesn't feel very realistic.
I'd recommend you to try this game if you see it on steam sale, it's not perfect but very good indeed. Also excellent soundtrack! 8/10

Alan Wake had a huge name before I even knew what it was about. Rumours and small spoils motivated me to play it for myself. On 1 May 2015 I finally set out on this adventure as a well known, cocky, used book writer who went on a retreat to Bright Falls in Washington, USA. It sets off on a slow pace and introduces you to all basic concepts and details.
The main goal of Alan Wake was to create an immersive movie or story with little effort needed from the viewer, they achieved this with simple controls and an easy difficulty to play on. Do not be fooled and think that the entire story is all fun and games, at the end of each episode everything would get intense, hordes of taken would appear leaving you to fight or flee for your life.
Categorised as a thriller I back the entire game, dwelling in silence with illuminating glare from the moon evolves slowly into a suspenseful walk with atmospheric music setting the tone of every scene. Even the classic jump scares are included, strolling through a home when suddenly a taken busts through the door charging you with al there is. Some were predictable and some were not, but balanced and not worn out.
Physical gameplay felt unnatural and sloppy but to be fair it was a conversion form Xbox to PC. Minor glitches like getting stuck on something or jumping and getting stuck but no big problems.
Graphics….. This was hard, reviewing in 2015 vs back in 2010 is quite a difference seeing that my GTX 760 made mincemeat of any graphical requirement it threw my way. Certain unpleasantness struck me in cinematics due to visible comers and edges, Alan’s Face his hands ect.
BUT
Comparing to other titles released in 2010 it seems like the quality of visuals were up to standard, titles like Mass Effect 2, Just Cause 2, Assassin’s creed Brotherhood also had some of these characteristics that feels unpleasant to the eyes.
This story was amazing and immersive…
At first they make you compare yourself to Alan, at this stage you would feel all his pain. Then they drop an unravelling bomb on you where you start to hate our Hero, after a while you start agreeing again and feel his drive, anger, hatred and determination to finish his adventure.
At the very end the unthinkable happens and they leave you on the biggest cliff-hanger ever created by mankind.
They later on released special episodes 1 and 2 which continues the story after the story, these were not as good as the main story but also deserves your attention.  It does not really enlighten you about happenings after and if you can shut off your entire brain and only receive entertainment through playing games, I would implore you to do this as the FINAL
did not give any closure and generated more hope than was needed.
Unfortunately it seems that Alan Wake 2 will not make an appearance in the future, Quantum break releasing exclusively to Xbox one will receive this title. Producers and directors feel that it is not within the age or time to make a new Title to this extremely awesome piece of art and creative immersion.
My next game would be Alan Wakes American Nightmare.
Hit the review section up to see may say in a months’ time.
FINAL VERDICT: ABSOLUTE YES, Add it to your rich-story category in your library.
