Now, first things first: playing Lincoln Clay feels great. You did a great job on the animations, handling and gameplay feeling in general. Lincoln does feel like a real badass.
Now secondly and most important: Is this supposed to be a gaming experience of the 21st century? I have 6 hours on the clock and I'm already bored. I was really looking forward to this game and I didn't join into the ♥♥♥♥♥torm about the 30fps. I wasn't pleased but it didn't ruin my experience. So I'm likely to forgive some stuff. But the way Mafia 3 is presented is repetitive and boring.
In detail:
- the police AI: you gotta be kidding me. I can run over people, speed and do whatever♥♥♥♥♥♥in front of a policeman he wouldn't do anything
- police needs ages to respond, I'm long gone by then.
- the combat AI is ridiculously stupid
- Police and the consequences I have to face when I'm going wild in the city have always been a crucial part of mafia games and makes them the way they are. I can start a shootout in the middle of the road and nobody responds
- the way I have to take back the city feels like running from checkpoint to checkpoint like in any damn far cry game.
- Story is good. Cinematics are awesome, why don't you make something out of it in the actual gameplay?
- I wanna have the feeling my businees grows. I wanna have a warehouse where I can see how my money stacks up
- it's all repetitive. Either I kill someone or take over a racket or drive like a maniac. Boring after a couple of hours
- A city is an organism. I expect from a 21st century game that my actions as a gangster have their consequences. It changes the city and me
- Hard difficulty is a walk in the park.
these are just some fast thoughts. I was really waiting for the game and now the disappointment is big. Thing is, Steam doesn't have something in the middle. I have to choose either positive or negative. I can't decide. It feels great to play Lincoln Clay. The shootouts and handling is a lot of fun. But it's not more than something for an hour in between. There is no vibrant city in which I run into stuff all along. Sry, not the big shot we all hoped for. Feels like you went over a check list for open world games implemented that stuff and then stopped thinking about it. Could've been something great. Especially with the story the game tells. The way it is presented in cinematics and the historic setting with all the racial issues is amazing and I would have loved to see it wrapped into an innovative game.

A mixed bag worth checking out.  Good for 10-20 hours, then grindy for another 10-30 depending on playstyle. For me it wasn't as dark as I expected, silly and 'cartoony' throughout.
Large random world, but only to provide variety on replay. Everything quest related is in a medium sized radius, beyond that there is nothing of interest. Three different biomes with a variety of flora and fauna, but begins to feel like a re-skin pretty quickly. Lots of different gear, appearance wise, but stats are the same throughout. Tier progression is very rapid, meaning the gear you spent an hour grinding mats for gets replaced 15 minutes later. The worst culprit is the way that damage scales exponentially, and gear is almost exclusively crafted through storyline obtained crafting stations resulting in a very linear experience. Lots of innuendo and slightly masked genital references.
Combat wasn't much fun to me, lots of running in a big circle kiting the mobs while pet attacks. Even lower level mobs can one or two shot you, so melee is a pain, and your ranged attacks have a long cool-down.
Still, the art is very nice, and the writing is often very good. (Not as good as the trailers, though.)

-Beautiful artstyle / animations
Cons:

Paladins is a fun and exhilarating experince which requires a lot of teamwork aswell as individual skill. While the game still has its imperfections, I feel that the gameplay and experience really outweigh them.
Recently, the devs introduced a new currency called essence which is used to purchase cards that allow you to builds decks that enhance a certain champions stats. The essence can be earned through playing the game or can be bought with real money. While a lot of people see this as a p2w system, I think it isnt TOO bad considering its not that hard to get the essence. You can still be just as good as a player with good cards even though your cards are sub-par.
The game is still in beta and the devs (Hi-Rez Studios) do definetly listen to the feedback and critiques of their playerbase. Just go have a look at the games subreddit. There are some UI bugs (mostly in the main menu) that an be easily fixed once the developers are noted of them.
The gameplay of Paladins is very fast paced, there are not many 1v1 duels, its mainly team fights. Your team is the single greatest weapon the game, if used properly, any game can be won.
Im excited to see the general direction of this game and I wish to see the community grow even larger than it is now. It has a real potential to be a great e sports game.
The only thing that can destroy this game is the developers, and I have full faith that they will improve the game to the best of their ability and they will always listen to player feedback.

I thought i should write a short review about this game.
I have played a couple of hours (50) and i can confirm that this game
is despite the public opinion against lootchests very good.
I was wondering about the good scores even though this game has loot chests.
In a matter fact the loot chests are just an addition to the gameplay.
There is no need for buying these because its just like a normal game shop like in animal crossing.
To be honest in animal crossing you dont need to pay with real money and here you do neither.
During all the gameplay i never felt once forced to buy any of these chests.
After explaining the chest system in my point of view, i will continue with list of postive and negative.
Positive
+ beautiful graphics, really detailed
+ personality of the orcs
+ new and better nemesis system
+ really difficult
+ more fluently fighting system
+ good story start
+ Dragons (come on that are dragons!)
+ all skills
+ you probably get enough XP and all skills until the end of the game
Negative
- good graphics needs good PC
- sometimes you dont really realise the different personalites of the orcs due to short conversations
- unprecisly hitbox when running or jumping (Especially with dragons it feel uncomfortable)
- ending which does not really meet my expectations
- XP are only given from quests or bosses
- skill system makes the beginning too difficult because even in late game the difficulty is worse.
- Not skipable sequences (activites from orks, conversations, fast restart button in some cases are missing)
- skills which should be activated simultaneous cannot be activated simultanous
- every item needs to get dismantled one by one
- the forcing of doing castle thingies if you wanna level higher, otherwise its really difficult to get more level
- Orks can have a higher level than you which means they cannot be recruited
- If you wanna have Legendary items over lvl 60 you need to find a legendary ork over lvl 60
Feedback/wishes from my side
- For Pc players an hotkey for changing the skills would be nice, it was really annoying opening this menu first bevor changing skills. (Example if i wanna summon a dragon, i need to switch from summon a caragor first)
- just make the castle conversations skipable
- easier menu to dismantle things
This is all the feedback i have.
Although there is a lot of negative feedback its just fine adjustmend which would make the game more fluently in my opinion
I can recommend the game because its still a fantastic game. Those who find the first part good will find this one probably good as well.

Spintires is a fun and unique offroad experience. Simple to understand but hard to master there are a variety of challenging maps and modes that can tailor the experience to the player's needs. Hardcore mode disables instant recovery options, requires the player to plan a supply network of support vehicles and makes tough stretches of road and river crossings extremely tense. The different attachments and modifications of the vehicles have realistic utility and are not just there for show.
If I had to pick one highlight from the game it's terrain deformation.... each surface reacts and deforms differently (sand, mud, gravel, concrete, packed dirt, grass, root covered forest floors) the detail is amazing. Ruts and trenches build up over time as the hulking Soviet era vehicles roll through, tilting and shifting with dynamic surfaces. There is a real sense of weight with the vehicles. Even the tire pressure is noticeable. Co-op online is rewarding and definitely useful while attempting to unlock achievements. Anyway, I don't want to be long winded – check out Spintires for a detailed, rewarding offroad experience.

Your robot named Enforcer... can be upgraded which is the only tactical part of the game as in what to upgrade when. You can upgrade your speed, jumping, max ammo and hp. You also can upgrade a variety of buff items to enhance them and also your limited ammo weapons (which is everything except your basic attack). My favorite weapon and I recommend maxxing it out first is the Mass Driver. It combines decent firing speed and accuracy of a rifle with the minor splash, aoe and penetration of say a grenade launcher. 1st upgrades to your robot I suggest are improved jump and some speed. To be fair it as an ok attempt to make a "shooter" but when ever a game series that is well established changed game play like this it usually turns out people hate it. People want same but different not different but similar.

Not a strategy game as said above!
GOTY 2012.

If you love big trucks and offroad driving for the sake of overcoming obstacles and heavy terrain with average speed of 100 meters / minute, you will love this game! If you admire old solid trucks from Soviet era that you can fix with just a hammer, it's a cherry on top. In contrast, if you are after BAJA race-like game then this is not what you're looking for (at least till modding community gets its hands on it properly).
Lookup some gameplay videos on youtube, e.g.

If you like what you see when others play it, you will enjoy the game.
-------------
Some details:
It is quite difficult even on "casual" settings and you need to think before you drive into something. It's prudent to check the game manual or some tutorials to find out how to use all wheels drive, differential lock and winch, otherwise you may end up stuck 10 seconds after leaving your garage.
Yes, the camera sucks and could do with some tweaks at least (which devs already promised to do), but even in it's current form you can live with it. It takes some getting used to but in the end you will learn how to tame it (I have tried just keyboard and mouse controls though).
It lasts to be an exciting challenge for some 15-20 hours of singleplayer (roughly the time it takes to complete all maps at causal diff.), after that it can get repetitive for some people (it's always: explore map + unlock goodies -> find easiest route -> make 2-4 trips with logs). I suppose you could repeat all that on Hard, but given that you will know the maps already and remember how to avoid mud traps... Hopefully we will see some more content added and also stuff from modding community that will extend the playability.
As for multiplayer, I haven't tried myself yet but from what I have seen on youtube it can be even more fun.
Other things that are slightly annoing but probably won't spoil your first 20 hours:
- You can't save progress on each map independently (devs promised to fix this though)
- Once you finish a map it resets and is "cloaked" again
- Multiplayer doesn't sync all sounds (will hopefully be fixed in future updates)
